column.value: So David and Abishai came to the people by night: and, behold, Saul lay sleeping within the trench, and his spear stuck in the ground at his head: but Abner and the people lay about him.

column.name: text
column.value: Then said Abishai to David, God hath delivered thy enemy into thy hand this day: now therefore let me smite him, I pray thee, with the spear even to the earth at once, and I will not {smite} him the second time.

column.name: text
column.value: And David said to Abishai, Destroy him not: for who can stretch forth his hand against the LORD'S anointed, and be guiltless?

column.name: text
column.value: David said furthermore, {As} the LORD liveth, the LORD shall smite him; or his day shall come to die; or he shall descend into battle, and perish.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD forbid that I should stretch forth my hand against the LORD'S anointed: but, I pray thee, take thou now the spear that {is} at his head, and the cruse of water, and let us go.

column.name: text
column.value: So David took the spear and the cruse of water from {beside} Saul's head; and they departed, and no man saw {it}, nor knew {it}, neither awoke: for they {were} all asleep; because a deep sleep from the LORD had fallen upon them.

column.name: text
column.value: Then David went over to the other side, and stood on the top of an hill afar off; a great space {being} between them:

column.name: text
column.value: And David cried to the people, and to Abner the son of Ner, saying, Answerest thou not, Abner? Then Abner answered and said, Who {art} thou {that} criest to the king?

column.name: text
column.value: And David said to Abner, {Art} not thou a {valiant} man? and who {is} like thee in Israel? why then hast thou not kept thy lord the king? for there came in one of the people to destroy the king thy lord.

column.name: text
column.value: This thing {is} not good that thou hast done. {As} the LORD liveth, ye {are} worthy to die, because ye have not kept your master, the LORD'S anointed. And now see where the king's spear {is}, and the cruse of water that {was} at his head.

column.name: text
column.value: And Saul knew David's voice, and said, {Is} this thy voice, my son David? And David said, {It is} my voice, my lord, O king.

column.name: text
column.value: And he said, Why doth my lord thus pursue his servant? for what have I done? or what evil {is} in my hand?

column.name: text
column.value: Now therefore, I pray thee, let my lord the king hear the words of his servant. If the LORD hath stirred thee up against me, let him accept an offering: but if {they are} the children of men, cursed {be} they before the LORD; for they have driven me out this day from abiding in the inheritance of the LORD, saying, Go, serve other gods.

column.name: text
column.value: Now therefore, let not my blood fall to the earth before the face of the LORD: for the king of Israel hath come out to seek a flea, as when one doth hunt a partridge in the mountains.

column.name: text
column.value: Then said Saul, I have sinned: return, my son David: for I will no more do thee harm, because my soul was precious in thy eyes this day: behold, I have played the fool, and have erred exceedingly.

column.name: text
column.value: And David answered and said, Behold the king's spear! and let one of the young men come over and take it.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD render to every man his righteousness and his faithfulness: for the LORD delivered thee into {my} hand to day, but I would not stretch forth my hand against the LORD'S anointed.

column.name: text
column.value: And, behold, as thy life was precious this day in my eyes, so let my life be precious in the eyes of the LORD, and let him deliver me out of all tribulation.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Saul said to David, Blessed {be} thou, my son David: thou shalt both do great {things}, and also shalt still prevail. So David went on his way, and Saul returned to his place.

column.name: text
column.value: And it came to pass, when Saul had returned from following the Philistines, that it was told to him, saying, Behold, David {is} in the wilderness of Engedi.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Saul took three thousand chosen men out of all Israel, and went to seek David and his men upon the rocks of the wild goats.

column.name: text
column.value: And he came to the sheepfolds by the way, where {was} a cave; and Saul went in to cover his feet: and David and his men remained in the sides of the cave.

column.name: text
column.value: And the men of David said to him, Behold the day of which the LORD said to thee, Behold, I will deliver thy enemy into thy hand, that thou mayest do to him as it shall seem good to thee. Then David arose, and secretly cut off the skirt of Saul's robe.

column.name: text
column.value: And it came to pass afterward, that David's heart smote him, because he had cut off Saul's skirt.

column.name: text
column.value: And he said to his men, The LORD forbid that I should do this thing to my master, the LORD'S anointed, to stretch forth my hand against him, seeing he {is} the anointed of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: So David restrained his servants with these words, and permitted them not to rise against Saul. But Saul rose out of the cave, and went on {his} way.

column.name: text
column.value: David also rose afterward, and went out of the cave, and cried after Saul, saying, My lord the king. And when Saul looked behind him, David stooped with his face to the earth, and bowed himself.

column.name: text
column.value: And David said to Saul, Why hearest thou men's words, saying, Behold, David seeketh thy harm?

column.name: text
column.value: Behold, this day thy eyes have seen how the LORD hath delivered thee to day into my hand in the cave: and {some} bade {me} kill thee: but {my eye} spared thee; and I said, I will not put forth my hand against my lord; for he {is} the LORD'S anointed.

column.name: text
column.value: Moreover, my father, see, yea, see the skirt of thy robe in my hand: for in that I cut off the skirt of thy robe, and killed thee not, know thou and see that {there is} neither evil nor transgression in my hand, and I have not sinned against thee; yet thou huntest my soul to take it.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD judge between me and thee, and the LORD avenge me of thee: but my hand shall not be upon thee.

column.name: text
column.value: As saith the proverb of the ancients, Wickedness proceedeth from the wicked: but my hand shall not be upon thee.

column.name: text
column.value: After whom is the king of Israel come out? after whom dost thou pursue? after a dead dog, after a flea.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD therefore be judge, and judge between me and thee, and see, and plead my cause, and deliver me out of thy hand.

column.name: text
column.value: And it came to pass, when David had finished speaking these words to Saul, that Saul said, {Is} this thy voice, my son David? And Saul lifted up his voice, and wept.

column.name: text
column.value: And he said to David, Thou {art} more righteous than I: for thou hast rewarded me with good, though I have rewarded thee with evil.

column.name: text
column.value: And thou hast showed this day how thou hast dealt with me: forasmuch as when the LORD had delivered me into thy hand, thou didst not kill me.

column.name: text
column.value: For if a man findeth his enemy, will he let him go away well? therefore the LORD reward thee with good for what thou hast done to me this day.

column.name: text
column.value: And now, behold, I know well that thou shalt surely be king, and that the kingdom of Israel shall be established in thy hand.

column.name: text
column.value: Swear now therefore to me by the LORD, that thou wilt not cut off my seed after me, and that thou wilt not destroy my name out of my father's house.

column.name: text
column.value: And David swore to Saul. And Saul went home; but David and his men went up to the strong hold.

column.name: text
column.value: And it came to pass in those days, that the Philistines gathered their armies together for warfare, to fight with Israel. And Achish said to David, Know thou assuredly, that thou shalt go out with me to battle, thou and thy men.

column.name: text
column.value: And David said to Achish, Surely thou shalt know what thy servant can do. And Achish said to David, Therefore will I make thee keeper of my head for ever.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Samuel was dead, and all Israel had lamented him, and buried him in Ramah, even in his own city. And Saul had put away those that were mediums, and the wizards, out of the land.

column.name: text
column.value: And the Philistines gathered themselves together, and came and encamped in Shunem: and Saul gathered all Israel together, and they encamped in Gilboa.

column.name: text
column.value: And when Saul saw the host of the Philistines, he was afraid, and his heart greatly trembled.

column.name: text
column.value: And when Saul enquired of the LORD, the LORD answered him not, neither by dreams, nor by Urim, nor by prophets.

column.name: text
column.value: Then said Saul to his servants, Seek me a woman that is a medium, that I may go to her, and enquire of her. And his servants said to him, Behold, {there is} a woman that hath a medium at Endor.

column.name: text
column.value: And Saul disguised himself, and put on other raiment, and he went, and two men with him, and they came to the woman by night: and he said, I pray thee, divine to me as a medium, and bring up for me, whom I shall name to thee.

column.name: text
column.value: And the woman said to him, Behold, thou knowest what Saul hath done, how he hath cut off those that are mediums, and the wizards, out of the land: Why then layest thou a snare for my life, to cause me to die?

column.name: text
column.value: And Saul swore to her by the LORD, saying, {As} the LORD liveth, there shall no punishment happen to thee for this thing.

column.name: text
column.value: Then said the woman, Whom shall I bring up to thee? And he said, Bring me up Samuel.

column.name: text
column.value: And when the woman saw Samuel, she cried with a loud voice: and the woman spoke to Saul, saying, Why hast thou deceived me? for thou {art} Saul.

column.name: text
column.value: And the king said to her, Be not afraid: for what sawest thou? And the woman said to Saul, I saw gods ascending out of the earth.

column.name: text
column.value: And he said to her, What is his form? And she said, An old man cometh up; and he {is} covered with a mantle. And Saul perceived that it {was} Samuel, and he stooped with {his} face to the ground, and bowed himself.

column.name: text
column.value: And Samuel said to Saul, Why hast thou disquieted me, to bring me up? And Saul answered, I am grievously distressed; for the Philistines make war against me, and God hath departed from me, and answereth me no more, neither by prophets, nor by dreams: therefore I have called thee, that thou mayest make known to me what I shall do.

column.name: text
column.value: Then said Samuel, Why then dost thou ask of me, seeing the LORD hath departed from thee, and hath become thy enemy?

column.name: text
column.value: And the LORD hath done to him, as he spoke by me: for the LORD hath torn the kingdom out of thy hand, and given it to thy neighbour, {even} to David:

column.name: text
column.value: Because thou didst not obey the voice of the LORD, nor execute his fierce wrath upon Amalek, therefore hath the LORD done this thing to thee this day.

column.name: text
column.value: Moreover the LORD will also deliver Israel with thee into the hand of the Philistines: and to morrow {shalt} thou and thy sons {be} with me: the LORD also shall deliver the host of Israel into the hand of the Philistines.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Saul fell immediately all along on the earth, and was exceedingly afraid, because of the words of Samuel: and there was no strength in him; for he had eaten no bread all the day, nor all the night.

column.name: text
column.value: And the woman came to Saul, and saw that he was greatly troubled, and said to him, Behold, thy handmaid hath obeyed thy voice, and I have put my life in my hand, and have hearkened to thy words which thou spoke to me.

column.name: text
column.value: Now therefore, I pray thee, hearken thou also to the voice of thy handmaid, and let me set a morsel of bread before thee; and eat, that thou mayest have strength, when thou goest on thy way.

column.name: text
column.value: But he refused, and said, I will not eat. But his servants, together with the woman, compelled him; and he hearkened to their voice. So he arose from the earth, and sat upon the bed.

column.name: text
column.value: And the woman had a fat calf in the house; and she hasted, and killed it, and took flour, and kneaded {it}, and baked unleavened bread from it:

column.name: text
column.value: And she brought {it} before Saul, and before his servants; and they ate. Then they arose, and went away that night.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the Philistines gathered together all their armies to Aphek: and the Israelites encamped by a fountain which {is} in Jezreel.

column.name: text
column.value: And the lords of the Philistines passed on by hundreds, and by thousands: but David and his men passed on in the rear with Achish.

column.name: text
column.value: Then said the princes of the Philistines, What {do} these Hebrews {here}? And Achish said to the princes of the Philistines, {Is} not this David, the servant of Saul the king of Israel, who hath been with me these days, or these years, and I have found no fault in him since he fell {to me} to this day?

column.name: text
column.value: And the princes of the Philistines were angry with him; and the princes of the Philistines said to him, Make this fellow return, that he may go again to his place which thou hast appointed him, and let him not go down with us to battle, lest in the battle he should be an adversary to us: for how should he reconcile himself to his master? {should it} not {be} with the heads of these men?

column.name: text
column.value: {Is} not this David, of whom they sang one to another in dances, saying, Saul slew his thousands, and David his ten thousands?

column.name: text
column.value: Then Achish called David, and said to him, Surely, {as} the LORD liveth, thou hast been upright, and thy going out and thy coming in with me in the host {is} good in my sight: for I have not found evil in thee from the day of thy coming to me to this day: nevertheless the lords favour thee not.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore now return, and go in peace, that thou displease not the lords of the Philistines.

column.name: text
column.value: And David said to Achish, But what have I done? and what hast thou found in thy servant so long as I have been with thee to this day, that I may not go and fight against the enemies of my lord the king?

column.name: text
column.value: And Achish answered and said to David, I know that thou {art} good in my sight, as an angel of God: however the princes of the Philistines have said, He shall not go up with us to the battle.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore now rise early in the morning with thy master's servants that are come with thee: and as soon as ye shall have risen early in the morning, and have light, depart.

column.name: text
column.value: So David and his men rose early to depart in the morning, to return into the land of the Philistines. And the Philistines went up to Jezreel.

column.name: text
column.value: And it came to pass, when David and his men were come to Ziklag on the third day, that the Amalekites had invaded the south, and Ziklag, and smitten Ziklag, and burned it with fire;

column.name: text
column.value: And had taken the women captives, that {were} in it: they slew not any, either great or small, but carried {them} away, and went on their way.

column.name: text
column.value: So David and his men came to the city, and, behold, {it was} burned with fire; and their wives, and their sons, and their daughters, were taken captives.

column.name: text
column.value: Then David and the people that {were} with him lifted up their voice and wept, until they had no more power to weep.

column.name: text
column.value: And David's two wives were taken captives, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess, and Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite.

column.name: text
column.value: And David was greatly distressed; for the people spoke of stoning him, because the soul of all the people was grieved, every man for his sons and for his daughters: but David encouraged himself in the LORD his God.

column.name: text
column.value: And David said to Abiathar the priest, Ahimelech's son, I pray thee, bring me here the ephod. And Abiathar brought there the ephod to David.

column.name: text
column.value: And David enquired of the LORD, saying, Shall I pursue this troop? shall I overtake them? And he answered him, Pursue: for thou shalt surely overtake {them}, and without fail recover {all}.

column.name: text
column.value: So David went, he and the six hundred men that {were} with him, and came to the brook Besor, where those that were left behind remained.

column.name: text
column.value: But David pursued, he and four hundred men: for two hundred abode behind, who were so faint that they could not go over the brook Besor.

column.name: text
column.value: And they found an Egyptian in the field, and brought him to David, and gave him bread, and he ate; and they made him drink water;

column.name: text
column.value: And they gave him a piece of a cake of figs, and two clusters of raisins: and when he had eaten, his spirit came again to him: for he had eaten no bread, nor drunk {any} water, three days and three nights.

column.name: text
column.value: And David said to him, To whom {belongest} thou? and from where {art} thou? And he said, I {am} a young man of Egypt, servant to an Amalekite; and my master left me, because three days ago I fell sick.

column.name: text
column.value: We made an invasion {upon} the south of the Cherethites, and upon {the land} which {belongeth} to Judah, and upon the south of Caleb; and we burned Ziklag with fire.

column.name: text
column.value: And David said to him, Canst thou bring me down to this company? And he said, Swear to me by God, that thou wilt neither kill me, nor deliver me into the hands of my master, and I will bring thee down to this company.

column.name: text
column.value: And when he had brought him down, behold, {they were} spread abroad upon all the earth, eating and drinking, and dancing, because of all the great spoil that they had taken from the land of the Philistines, and from the land of Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: And David smote them from the twilight even to the evening of the next day: and there escaped not a man of them, except four hundred young men, who rode upon camels, and fled.

column.name: text
column.value: And David recovered all that the Amalekites had carried away: and David rescued his two wives.

column.name: text
column.value: And there was nothing lacking to them, neither small nor great, neither sons nor daughters, neither spoil, nor any {thing} that they had taken to them: David recovered all.

column.name: text
column.value: And David took all the flocks and the herds, {which} they drove before those {other} cattle, and said, This {is} David's spoil.

column.name: text
column.value: And David came to the two hundred men, who were so faint that they could not follow David, whom they had made also to abide at the brook Besor: and they went forth to meet David, and to meet the people that {were} with him: and when David came near to the people, he greeted them.

column.name: text
column.value: Then answered all the wicked and worthless men, of those that went with David, and said, Because they went not with us, we will not give them {any} of the spoil that we have recovered, except to every man his wife and his children, that they may lead {them} away, and depart.

column.name: text
column.value: Then said David, Ye shall not do so, my brethren, with that which the LORD hath given us, who hath preserved us, and delivered the company that came against us into our hand.

column.name: text
column.value: For who will hearken to you in this matter? but as his part {is} that goeth down to the battle, so {shall} his part {be} that tarrieth by the baggage: they shall divide alike.

column.name: text
column.value: And it was {so} from that day onward, that he made it a statute and an ordinance for Israel to this day.

column.name: text
column.value: And when David came to Ziklag, he sent of the spoil to the elders of Judah, {even} to his friends, saying, Behold a present for you of the spoil of the enemies of the LORD;

column.name: text
column.value: To {them} who {were} in Bethel, and to {them} who {were} in south Ramoth, and to {them} who {were} in Jattir,

column.name: text
column.value: And to {them} who {were} in Aroer, and to {them} who {were} in Siphmoth, and to {them} who {were} in Eshtemoa,

column.name: text
column.value: And to {them} who {were} in Rachal, and to {them} who {were} in the cities of the Jerahmeelites, and to {them} who {were} in the cities of the Kenites,

column.name: text
column.value: And to {them} who {were} in Hormah, and to {them} who {were} in Chorashan, and to {them} who {were} in Athach,

column.name: text
column.value: And to {them} who {were} in Hebron, and to all the places where David himself and his men were accustomed to resort.

column.name: text
column.value: And Samuel died; and all the Israelites were gathered together, and lamented him, and buried him in his house at Ramah. And David arose, and went down to the wilderness of Paran.

column.name: text
column.value: And {there was} a man in Maon, whose possessions {were} in Carmel; and the man {was} very great, and he had three thousand sheep, and a thousand goats: and he was shearing his sheep in Carmel.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the name of the man {was} Nabal; and the name of his wife Abigail: and {she was} a woman of good understanding, and of a beautiful countenance: but the man {was} churlish and evil in his doings; and he {was} of the house of Caleb.

column.name: text
column.value: And David heard in the wilderness that Nabal was shearing his sheep.

column.name: text
column.value: And David sent ten young men, and David said to the young men, Go up to Carmel, and go to Nabal, and greet him in my name:

column.name: text
column.value: And thus shall ye say to him that liveth {in prosperity}, Peace {be} both to thee, and peace {be} to thy house, and peace {be} to all that thou hast.

column.name: text
column.value: And now I have heard that thou hast shearers: now thy shepherds who were with us, we hurt them not, neither was there any thing missing to them, all the while they were in Carmel.

column.name: text
column.value: Ask thy young men, and they will show thee. Therefore let the young men find favour in thy eyes: for we come in a good day: give, I pray thee, whatever cometh to thy hand to thy servants, and to thy son David.

column.name: text
column.value: And when David's young men came, they spoke to Nabal in the name of David, according to all these words, and ceased.

column.name: text
column.value: And Nabal answered David's servants, and said, Who {is} David? and who {is} the son of Jesse? there are many servants in these days that break away every man from his master.

column.name: text
column.value: Shall I then take my bread, and my water, and my flesh that I have killed for my shearers, and give {it} to men, whom I know not from where they {are}?

column.name: text
column.value: So David's young men turned their way, and went again, and came and told him all these sayings.

column.name: text
column.value: And David said to his men, Gird ye on every man his sword. And they girded on every man his sword; and David also girded on his sword: and there went up after David about four hundred men; and two hundred abode by the baggage.

column.name: text
column.value: But one of the young men told Abigail, Nabal's wife, saying, Behold, David sent messengers from the wilderness to greet our master; and he railed at them.

column.name: text
column.value: But the men {were} very good to us, and we were not hurt, neither missed we any thing, as long as we were conversant with them, when we were in the fields:

column.name: text
column.value: They were a wall to us both by night and day, all the while we were with them keeping the sheep.

column.name: text
column.value: Now therefore know and consider what thou wilt do; for evil is determined against our master, and against all his household: for he {is such} a worthless man, that {a man} cannot speak to him.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Abigail made haste, and took two hundred loaves, and two bottles of wine, and five sheep ready dressed, and five measures of roasted {grain}, and an hundred clusters of raisins, and two hundred cakes of figs, and laid {them} on donkeys.

column.name: text
column.value: And she said to her servants, Go on before me; behold, I come after you. But she told not her husband Nabal.

column.name: text
column.value: And it was {so, as} she rode on the donkey, that she came down by the covert of the hill, and, behold, David and his men came down toward her; and she met them.

column.name: text
column.value: Now David had said, Surely in vain have I kept all that this {fellow} hath in the wilderness, so that nothing was missed of all that {pertained} to him: and he hath repaid me evil for good.

column.name: text
column.value: So and more also do God to the enemies of David, if I leave of all that {pertain} to him by the morning light any male person.

column.name: text
column.value: And when Abigail saw David, she hasted, and got off the donkey, and fell before David on her face, and bowed herself to the ground,

column.name: text
column.value: And fell at his feet, and said, Upon me, my lord, {upon} me {let this} iniquity {be}: and let thy handmaid, I pray thee, speak in thy hearing, and hear the words of thy handmaid.

column.name: text
column.value: Let not my lord, I pray thee, regard this worthless man, {even} Nabal: for as his name {is}, so {is} he; Nabal {is} his name, and folly {is} with him: but I thy handmaid saw not the young men of my lord, whom thou didst send.

column.name: text
column.value: Now therefore, my lord, {as} the LORD liveth, and {as} thy soul liveth, seeing the LORD hath withheld thee from coming to {shed} blood, and from avenging thyself with thy own hand, now let thy enemies, and they that seek evil to my lord, be as Nabal.

column.name: text
column.value: And now this blessing which thy handmaid hath brought to my lord, let it even be given to the young men that follow my lord.

column.name: text
column.value: I pray thee, forgive the trespass of thy handmaid: for the LORD will certainly make my lord a sure house; because my lord fighteth the battles of the LORD, and evil hath not been found in thee {all} thy days.

column.name: text
column.value: Yet a man hath risen to pursue thee, and to seek thy soul: but the soul of my lord shall be bound in the bundle of life with the LORD thy God; and the souls of thy enemies, them shall he sling out, {as from} the middle of a sling.

column.name: text
column.value: And it shall come to pass, when the LORD shall have done to my lord according to all the good that he hath spoken concerning thee, and shall have appointed thee ruler over Israel;

column.name: text
column.value: That this shall be no grief to thee, nor offence of heart to my lord, either that thou hast shed blood without cause, or that my lord hath avenged himself: but when the LORD shall have dealt well with my lord, then remember thy handmaid.

column.name: text
column.value: And David said to Abigail, Blessed {be} the LORD God of Israel, who sent thee this day to meet me:

column.name: text
column.value: And blessed {be} thy advice, and blessed {be} thou, who hast kept me this day from coming to {shed} blood, and from avenging myself with my own hand.

column.name: text
column.value: For in very deed, {as} the LORD God of Israel liveth, who hath kept me back from hurting thee, except thou hadst hasted and come to meet me, surely there had not been left to Nabal by the morning light any male person.

column.name: text
column.value: So David received from her hand {that} which she had brought him, and said to her, Return in peace to thy house; see, I have hearkened to thy voice, and have accepted thy person.

column.name: text
column.value: And Abigail came to Nabal; and, behold, he held a feast in his house, like the feast of a king; and Nabal's heart {was} merry within him, for he {was} very drunk: therefore she told him nothing, less or more, until the morning light.

column.name: text
column.value: But it came to pass in the morning, when the wine had left Nabal, and his wife had told him these things, that his heart died within him, and he became {as} a stone.

column.name: text
column.value: And it came to pass about ten days {after}, that the LORD smote Nabal, that he died.

column.name: text
column.value: And when David heard that Nabal was dead, he said, Blessed {be} the LORD, that hath pleaded the cause of my reproach from the hand of Nabal, and hath kept his servant from evil: for the LORD hath returned the wickedness of Nabal upon his own head. And David sent and talked with Abigail, to take her to himself for a wife.

column.name: text
column.value: And when the servants of David had come to Abigail to Carmel, they spoke to her, saying, David hath sent us to thee, to take thee to him for a wife.

column.name: text
column.value: And she arose, and bowed herself on {her} face to the earth, and said, Behold, {let} thy handmaid {be} a servant to wash the feet of the servants of my lord.

column.name: text
column.value: And Abigail hasted, and arose, and rode upon a donkey, with five damsels of hers that went after her; and she went after the messengers of David, and became his wife.

column.name: text
column.value: David also took Ahinoam of Jezreel; and they were also both of them his wives.

column.name: text
column.value: But Saul had given Michal his daughter, David's wife, to Phalti the son of Laish, who {was} of Gallim.

column.name: text
column.value: Now it came to pass after the death of Saul, when David had returned from the slaughter of the Amalekites, and David had abode two days in Ziklag;

column.name: text
column.value: It came even to pass on the third day, that, behold, a man came out of the camp from Saul with his clothes torn, and earth upon his head: and {so} it was, when he came to David, that he fell to the earth, and did obeisance.

column.name: text
column.value: And David said to him, From where comest thou? And he said to him, Out of the camp of Israel have I escaped.

column.name: text
column.value: And David said to him, How went the matter? I pray thee, tell me. And he answered, That the people have fled from the battle, and many of the people also have fallen and are dead; and Saul and Jonathan his son are dead also.

column.name: text
column.value: And David said to the young man that told him, How knowest thou that Saul and Jonathan his son are dead?

column.name: text
column.value: And the young man that told him said, As I happened by chance upon mount Gilboa, behold, Saul leaned upon his spear; and, lo, the chariots and horsemen followed hard after him.

column.name: text
column.value: And when he looked behind him, he saw me, and called to me. And I answered, Here {am} I.

column.name: text
column.value: And he said to me, Who {art} thou? And I answered him, I {am} an Amalekite.

column.name: text
column.value: He said to me again, Stand, I pray thee, upon me, and slay me: for anguish is come upon me, because my life {is} yet whole in me.

column.name: text
column.value: So I stood upon him, and slew him, because I was sure that he could not live after that he had fallen: and I took the crown that {was} upon his head, and the bracelet that {was} on his arm, and have brought them here to my lord.

column.name: text
column.value: Then David took hold on his clothes, and tore them; and likewise all the men that {were} with him:

column.name: text
column.value: And they mourned, and wept, and fasted until evening, for Saul, and for Jonathan his son, and for the people of the LORD, and for the house of Israel; because they had fallen by the sword.

column.name: text
column.value: And David said to the young man that told him, From where {art} thou? And he answered, I {am} the son of a stranger, an Amalekite.

column.name: text
column.value: And David said to him, How wast thou not afraid to stretch forth thy hand to destroy the LORD'S anointed?

column.name: text
column.value: And David called one of the young men, and said, Go near, {and} fall upon him. And he smote him that he died.

column.name: text
column.value: And David said to him, Thy blood {be} upon thy head; for thy mouth hath testified against thee, saying, I have slain the LORD'S anointed.

column.name: text
column.value: And David lamented with this lamentation over Saul and over Jonathan his son:

column.name: text
column.value: (Also he told them to teach the children of Judah {the use of} the bow: behold, {it is} written in the book of Jasher.)

column.name: text
column.value: Thy glory, O Israel is slain upon thy high places: how are the mighty fallen!

column.name: text
column.value: Tell {it} not in Gath, proclaim {it} not in the streets of Askelon; lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice, lest the daughters of the uncircumcised triumph.

column.name: text
column.value: Ye mountains of Gilboa, {let there be} no dew, neither rain, upon you, nor fields of offerings: for there the shield of the mighty is vilely cast away, the shield of Saul, {as though he had} not {been} anointed with oil.

column.name: text
column.value: From the blood of the slain, from the fat of the mighty, the bow of Jonathan turned not back, and the sword of Saul returned not empty.

column.name: text
column.value: Saul and Jonathan {were} lovely and pleasant in their lives, and in their death they were not divided: they were swifter than eagles, they were stronger than lions.

column.name: text
column.value: Ye daughters of Israel, weep over Saul, who clothed you in scarlet, with {other} delights, who put ornaments of gold upon your apparel.

column.name: text
column.value: How are the mighty fallen in the midst of the battle! O Jonathan, {thou wast} slain in thy high places.

column.name: text
column.value: I am distressed for thee, my brother Jonathan: very pleasant hast thou been to me: thy love to me was wonderful, passing the love of women.

column.name: text
column.value: How have the mighty fallen, and the weapons of war perished!

column.name: text
column.value: And it came to pass after this, that David enquired of the LORD, saying, Shall I go up into any of the cities of Judah? And the LORD said to him, Go up. And David said, Where shall I go up? And he said, To Hebron.

column.name: text
column.value: So David went up there, and his two wives also, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess, and Abigail Nabal's wife the Carmelite.

column.name: text
column.value: And his men that {were} with him did David bring up, every man with his household: and they dwelt in the cities of Hebron.

column.name: text
column.value: And the men of Judah came, and there they anointed David king over the house of Judah. And they told David, saying, {That} the men of Jabeshgilead {were they} that buried Saul.

column.name: text
column.value: And David sent messengers to the men of Jabeshgilead, and said to them, Blessed {be} ye of the LORD, that ye have shown this kindness to your lord, {even} to Saul, and have buried him.

column.name: text
column.value: And now the LORD show kindness and truth to you: and I also will repay you this kindness, because ye have done this thing.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore now let your hands be strengthened, and be ye valiant: for your master Saul is dead, and also the house of Judah have anointed me king over them.

column.name: text
column.value: But Abner the son of Ner, captain of Saul's host, took Ishbosheth the son of Saul, and brought him over to Mahanaim;

column.name: text
column.value: And he made him king over Gilead, and over the Ashurites, and over Jezreel, and over Ephraim, and over Benjamin, and over all Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: Ishbosheth Saul's son {was} forty years old when he began to reign over Israel, and he reigned two years. But the house of Judah followed David.

column.name: text
column.value: And the time that David was king in Hebron over the house of Judah was seven years and six months.

column.name: text
column.value: And Abner the son of Ner, and the servants of Ishbosheth the son of Saul, went out from Mahanaim to Gibeon.

column.name: text
column.value: And Joab the son of Zeruiah, and the servants of David, went out, and met together by the pool of Gibeon: and they sat down, the one on the one side of the pool, and the other on the other side of the pool.

column.name: text
column.value: And Abner said to Joab, Let the young men now arise, and fight before us. And Joab said, Let them arise.

column.name: text
column.value: Then there arose and went over by number twelve of Benjamin, who {pertained} to Ishbosheth the son of Saul, and twelve of the servants of David.

column.name: text
column.value: And they caught every one his opponent by the head, and {thrust} his sword in his opponent's side; so they fell down together: therefore that place was called Helkathhazzurim, which {is} in Gibeon.

column.name: text
column.value: And there was a very fierce battle that day; and Abner was smitten, and the men of Israel, before the servants of David.

column.name: text
column.value: And there were three sons of Zeruiah there, Joab, and Abishai, and Asahel: and Asahel {was as} light of foot as a wild roe.

column.name: text
column.value: And Asahel pursued after Abner; and in going he turned not to the right hand nor to the left from following Abner.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Abner looked behind him, and said, {Art} thou Asahel? And he answered, I {am}.

column.name: text
column.value: And Abner said to him, Turn thee aside to thy right hand or to thy left, and lay hold on one of the young men, and take to thee his armour. But Asahel would not turn aside from following him.

column.name: text
column.value: And Abner said again to Asahel, Turn thee aside from following me: why should I smite thee to the ground? how then should I hold up my face to Joab thy brother?

column.name: text
column.value: But he refused to turn aside: therefore Abner with the blunt end of the spear smote him under the fifth {rib}, that the spear came out behind him; and he fell down there, and died in the same place: and it came to pass, {that} as many as came to the place where Asahel fell down and died stood still.

column.name: text
column.value: Joab also and Abishai pursued Abner: and the sun went down when they had come to the hill of Ammah, that {lieth} before Giah by the way of the wilderness of Gibeon.

column.name: text
column.value: And the children of Benjamin gathered themselves together after Abner, and became one troop, and stood on the top of an hill.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Abner called to Joab, and said, Shall the sword devour for ever? knowest thou not that it will be bitterness in the latter end? how long shall it be then, before thou wilt bid the people return from following their brethren?

column.name: text
column.value: And Joab said, {As} God liveth, unless thou hadst spoken, surely then in the morning the people had gone up every one from following his brother.

column.name: text
column.value: So Joab blew a trumpet, and all the people stood still, and pursued Israel no more, neither fought they any more.

column.name: text
column.value: And Abner and his men walked all that night through the plain, and passed over Jordan, and went through all Bithron, and they came to Mahanaim.

column.name: text
column.value: And Joab returned from following Abner: and when he had gathered all the people together, there lacked of David's servants nineteen men and Asahel.

column.name: text
column.value: But the servants of David had smitten of Benjamin, and of Abner's men, {so that} three hundred and sixty men died.

column.name: text
column.value: And they took up Asahel, and buried him in the sepulchre of his father, which {was in} Bethlehem. And Joab and his men went all night, and they came to Hebron at break of day.

column.name: text
column.value: Now there was long war between the house of Saul and the house of David: but David grew stronger and stronger, and the house of Saul became weaker and weaker.

column.name: text
column.value: And to David were sons born in Hebron: and his firstborn was Amnon, of Ahinoam the Jezreelitess;

column.name: text
column.value: And his second, Chileab, of Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite; and the third, Absalom the son of Maacah the daughter of Talmai king of Geshur;

column.name: text
column.value: And the fourth, Adonijah the son of Haggith; and the fifth, Shephatiah the son of Abital;

column.name: text
column.value: And the sixth, Ithream, by Eglah David's wife. These were born to David in Hebron.

column.name: text
column.value: And it came to pass, while there was war between the house of Saul and the house of David, that Abner made himself strong for the house of Saul.

column.name: text
column.value: And Saul had a concubine, whose name {was} Rizpah, the daughter of Aiah: and {Ishbosheth} said to Abner, Why hast thou gone in to my father's concubine?

column.name: text
column.value: Then was Abner very angry for the words of Ishbosheth, and said, {Am} I a dog's head, who against Judah do show kindness this day to the house of Saul thy father, to his brethren, and to his friends, and have not delivered thee into the hand of David, that thou chargest me to day with a fault concerning this woman?

column.name: text
column.value: So do God to Abner, and more also, except, as the LORD hath sworn to David, even so I do to him;

column.name: text
column.value: To pass on the kingdom from the house of Saul, and to set up the throne of David over Israel and over Judah, from Dan even to Beersheba.

column.name: text
column.value: And he could not answer Abner a word again, because he feared him.

column.name: text
column.value: And Abner sent messengers to David on his behalf, saying, Whose {is} the land? saying {also}, Make thy league with me, and, behold, my hand {shall be} with thee, to bring about all Israel to thee.

column.name: text
column.value: And he said, Well; I will make a league with thee: but one thing I require of thee, that is, Thou shalt not see my face, except thou shalt first bring Michal Saul's daughter, when thou comest to see my face.

column.name: text
column.value: And David sent messengers to Ishbosheth Saul's son, saying, Deliver to {me} my wife Michal, whom I betrothed to me for an hundred foreskins of the Philistines.

column.name: text
column.value: And Ishbosheth sent, and took her from {her} husband, {even} from Phaltiel the son of Laish.

column.name: text
column.value: And her husband went with her weeping behind her to Bahurim. Then said Abner to him, Go, return. And he returned.

column.name: text
column.value: And Abner had communication with the elders of Israel, saying, Ye sought for David in times past {to be} king over you:

column.name: text
column.value: Now then do {it}: for the LORD hath spoken of David, saying, By the hand of my servant David I will save my people Israel from the hand of the Philistines, and from the hand of all their enemies.

column.name: text
column.value: And Abner also spoke in the ears of Benjamin: and Abner went also to speak in the ears of David in Hebron all that seemed good to Israel, and that seemed good to the whole house of Benjamin.

column.name: text
column.value: So Abner came to David in Hebron, and twenty men with him. And David made Abner and the men that {were} with him a feast.

column.name: text
column.value: And Abner said to David, I will arise and go, and will gather all Israel to my lord the king, that they may make a league with thee, and that thou mayest reign over all that thy heart desireth. And David sent Abner away; and he went in peace.

column.name: text
column.value: And, behold, the servants of David and Joab came from {pursuing} a troop, and brought in a great spoil with them: but Abner {was} not with David in Hebron; for he had sent him away, and he had gone in peace.

column.name: text
column.value: When Joab and all the host that {was} with him had come, they told Joab, saying, Abner the son of Ner came to the king, and he hath sent him away, and he hath gone in peace.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Joab came to the king, and said, What hast thou done? behold, Abner came to thee; why {is} it {that} thou hast sent him away, and he is quite gone?

column.name: text
column.value: Thou knowest Abner the son of Ner, that he came to deceive thee, and to know thy going out and thy coming in, and to know all that thou doest.

column.name: text
column.value: And when Joab had come out from David, he sent messengers after Abner, who brought him again from the well of Sirah: but David knew {it} not.

column.name: text
column.value: And when Abner had returned to Hebron, Joab took him aside in the gate to speak with him quietly, and smote him there under the fifth {rib}, that he died, for the blood of Asahel his brother.

column.name: text
column.value: And afterward when David heard {it}, he said, I and my kingdom {are} guiltless before the LORD for ever from the blood of Abner the son of Ner:

column.name: text
column.value: Let it rest on the head of Joab, and on all his father's house; and let there never cease from the house of Joab one that hath an issue, or that is a leper, or that leaneth on a staff, or that falleth on the sword, or that lacketh bread.

column.name: text
column.value: So Joab and Abishai his brother slew Abner, because he had slain their brother Asahel at Gibeon in the battle.

column.name: text
column.value: And David said to Joab, and to all the people that {were} with him, Rend your clothes, and gird yourselves with sackcloth, and mourn before Abner. And king David {himself} followed the bier.

column.name: text
column.value: And they buried Abner in Hebron: and the king lifted up his voice, and wept at the grave of Abner; and all the people wept.

column.name: text
column.value: And the king lamented over Abner, and said, Died Abner as a fool dieth?

column.name: text
column.value: Thy hands {were} not bound, nor thy feet put into fetters: as a man falleth before wicked men, {so} fellest thou. And all the people wept again over him.

column.name: text
column.value: And when all the people came to cause David to eat food while it was yet day, David swore, saying, So do God to me, and more also, if I taste bread, or any thing else, till the sun is down.

column.name: text
column.value: And all the people took notice {of it}, and it pleased them: as whatever the king did pleased all the people.

column.name: text
column.value: For all the people and all Israel understood that day that it was not of the king to slay Abner the son of Ner.

column.name: text
column.value: And the king said to his servants, Know ye not that there hath a prince and a great man fallen this day in Israel?

column.name: text
column.value: And I {am} this day weak, though anointed king; and these men the sons of Zeruiah {are} too hard for me: the LORD shall reward the doer of evil according to his wickedness.

column.name: text
column.value: And when Saul's son heard that Abner was dead in Hebron, his hands were feeble, and all the Israelites were troubled.

column.name: text
column.value: And Saul's son had two men {that were} captains of bands: the name of the one {was} Baanah, and the name of the other Rechab, the sons of Rimmon a Beerothite, of the children of Benjamin: (for Beeroth also was reckoned to Benjamin:

column.name: text
column.value: And the Beerothites fled to Gittaim, and have been sojourners there until this day.)

column.name: text
column.value: And Jonathan, Saul's son, had a son {that was} lame of {his} feet. He was five years old when the tidings came of Saul and Jonathan out of Jezreel, and his nurse took him up, and fled: and it came to pass, as she made haste to flee, that he fell, and became lame. And his name {was} Mephibosheth.

column.name: text
column.value: And the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, Rechab and Baanah, went, and came about the heat of the day to the house of Ishbosheth, who lay on a bed at noon.

column.name: text
column.value: And they came there into the midst of the house, {as though} they would have fetched wheat; and they smote him under the fifth {rib}: and Rechab and Baanah his brother escaped.

column.name: text
column.value: For when they came into the house, he lay on his bed in his bedchamber, and they smote him, and slew him, and beheaded him, and took his head, and went away through the plain all night.

column.name: text
column.value: And they brought the head of Ishbosheth to David to Hebron, and said to the king, Behold the head of Ishbosheth the son of Saul thy enemy, who sought thy life; and the LORD hath avenged my lord the king this day of Saul, and of his seed.

column.name: text
column.value: And David answered Rechab and Baanah his brother, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, and said to them, {As} the LORD liveth, who hath redeemed my soul out of all adversity,

column.name: text
column.value: When one told me, saying, Behold, Saul is dead, thinking to have brought good tidings, I took hold of him, and slew him in Ziklag, who {thought} that I would have given him a reward for his tidings:

column.name: text
column.value: How much more, when wicked men have slain a righteous person in his own house upon his bed? shall I not therefore now require his blood of your hand, and take you away from the earth?

column.name: text
column.value: And David commanded his young men, and they slew them, and cut off their hands and their feet, and hanged {them} over the pool in Hebron. But they took the head of Ishbosheth, and buried {it} in the sepulchre of Abner in Hebron.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the Philistines fought against Israel: and the men of Israel fled from before the Philistines, and fell down slain in mount Gilboa.

column.name: text
column.value: And the Philistines followed hard upon Saul and upon his sons; and the Philistines slew Jonathan, and Abinadab, and Malchishua, Saul's sons.

column.name: text
column.value: And the battle went heavily against Saul, and the archers hit him; and he was grievously wounded by the archers.

column.name: text
column.value: Then said Saul to his armourbearer, Draw thy sword, and thrust me through with it; lest these uncircumcised should come and thrust me through, and abuse me. But his armourbearer would not; for he was exceedingly afraid. Therefore Saul took a sword, and fell upon it.

column.name: text
column.value: And when his armourbearer saw that Saul was dead, he fell likewise upon his sword, and died with him.

column.name: text
column.value: So Saul died, and his three sons, and his armourbearer, and all his men, that same day together.

column.name: text
column.value: And when the men of Israel that {were} on the other side of the valley, and {they} that {were} on the other side of Jordan, saw that the men of Israel fled, and that Saul and his sons were dead, they forsook the cities, and fled; and the Philistines came and dwelt in them.

column.name: text
column.value: And it came to pass on the next day, when the Philistines came to strip the slain, that they found Saul and his three sons fallen in mount Gilboa.

column.name: text
column.value: And they cut off his head, and stripped off his armour, and sent {them} around the land of the Philistines, to proclaim {it in} the house of their idols, and among the people.

column.name: text
column.value: And they put his armour in the house of Ashtaroth: and they fastened his body to the wall of Bethshan.

column.name: text
column.value: And when the inhabitants of Jabeshgilead heard of that which the Philistines had done to Saul;

column.name: text
column.value: All the valiant men arose, and went all night, and took the body of Saul and the bodies of his sons from the wall of Bethshan, and came to Jabesh, and burnt them there.

column.name: text
column.value: And they took their bones, and buried {them} under a tree at Jabesh, and fasted seven days.

column.name: text
column.value: Then came all the tribes of Israel to David to Hebron, and spoke, saying, Behold, we {are} thy bone and thy flesh.

column.name: text
column.value: Also in time past, when Saul was king over us, thou wast he that leddest out and broughtest in Israel: and the LORD said to thee, Thou shalt feed my people Israel, and thou shalt be a captain over Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: So all the elders of Israel came to the king to Hebron; and king David made a league with them in Hebron before the LORD: and they anointed David king over Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: David {was} thirty years old when he began to reign, {and} he reigned forty years.

column.name: text
column.value: In Hebron he reigned over Judah seven years and six months: and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty and three years over all Israel and Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: And the king and his men went to Jerusalem to the Jebusites, the inhabitants of the land: who spoke to David, saying, Except thou shalt take away the blind and the lame, thou shalt not come in here: thinking, David cannot come in there.

column.name: text
column.value: Nevertheless David took the strong hold of Zion: the same {is} the city of David.

column.name: text
column.value: And David said on that day, Whoever getteth up to the gutter, and smiteth the Jebusites, and the lame and the blind, {that are} hated by David's soul, {he shall be chief and captain}. Therefore they said, The blind and the lame shall not come into the house.

column.name: text
column.value: So David dwelt in the fort, and called it the city of David. And David built around from Millo and inward.

column.name: text
column.value: And David went on, and grew great, and the LORD God of hosts {was} with him.

column.name: text
column.value: And Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, and cedar trees, and carpenters, and masons: and they built David an house.

column.name: text
column.value: And David perceived that the LORD had established him king over Israel, and that he had exalted his kingdom for his people Israel's sake.

column.name: text
column.value: And David took more concubines and wives out of Jerusalem, after he had come from Hebron: and there were yet sons and daughters born to David.

column.name: text
column.value: And these {are} the names of those that were born to him in Jerusalem; Shammua, and Shobab, and Nathan, and Solomon,

column.name: text
column.value: Ibhar also, and Elishua, and Nepheg, and Japhia,

column.name: text
column.value: And Elishama, and Eliada, and Eliphalet.

column.name: text
column.value: But when the Philistines heard that they had anointed David king over Israel, all the Philistines came up to seek David; and David heard {of it}, and went down to the strong hold.

column.name: text
column.value: The Philistines also came and spread themselves in the valley of Rephaim.

column.name: text
column.value: And David enquired of the LORD, saying, Shall I go up to the Philistines? wilt thou deliver them into my hand? And the LORD said to David, Go up: for I will certainly deliver the Philistines into thy hand.

column.name: text
column.value: And David came to Baalperazim, and David smote them there, and said, The LORD hath broken forth upon my enemies before me, as the breach of waters. Therefore he called the name of that place Baalperazim.

column.name: text
column.value: And there they left their images, and David and his men burned them.

column.name: text
column.value: And the Philistines came yet again, and spread themselves in the valley of Rephaim.

column.name: text
column.value: And when David enquired of the LORD, he said, Thou shalt not go up; {but} make a circuit behind them, and come upon them in front of the mulberry trees.

column.name: text
column.value: And let it be, when thou hearest the sound of marching in the tops of the mulberry trees, that then thou shalt bestir thyself: for then shall the LORD go out before thee, to smite the host of the Philistines.

column.name: text
column.value: And David did so, as the LORD had commanded him; and smote the Philistines from Geba until thou comest to Gazer.

column.name: text
column.value: And it came to pass, when the king sat in his house, and the LORD had given him rest on every side from all his enemies;

column.name: text
column.value: That the king said to Nathan the prophet, See now, I dwell in an house of cedar, but the ark of God dwelleth within curtains.

column.name: text
column.value: And Nathan said to the king, Go, do all that {is} in thy heart; for the LORD {is} with thee.

column.name: text
column.value: And it came to pass that night, that the word of the LORD came to Nathan, saying,

column.name: text
column.value: Go and tell my servant David, Thus saith the LORD, Shalt thou build me an house for me to dwell in?

column.name: text
column.value: Though I have not dwelt in {any} house since the time that I brought the children of Israel out of Egypt, even to this day, but have walked in a tent and in a tabernacle.

column.name: text
column.value: In all {the places} in which I have walked with all the children of Israel have I spoken a word with any of the tribes of Israel, whom I commanded to feed my people Israel, saying, Why do ye not build me an house of cedar?

column.name: text
column.value: Now therefore so shalt thou say to my servant David, Thus saith the LORD of hosts, I took thee from the sheepfold, from following the sheep, to be ruler over my people, over Israel:

column.name: text
column.value: And I was with thee wherever thou wentest, and have cut off all thy enemies out of thy sight, and have made thee a great name, like the name of the great {men} that {are} in the earth.

column.name: text
column.value: Moreover I will appoint a place for my people Israel, and will plant them, that they may dwell in a place of their own, and move no more; neither shall the children of wickedness afflict them any more, as in times past,

column.name: text
column.value: And as since the time that I commanded judges {to be} over my people Israel, and have caused thee to rest from all thy enemies. Also the LORD telleth thee that he will make thee an house.

column.name: text
column.value: And when thy days shall be fulfilled, and thou shalt sleep with thy fathers, I will set up thy seed after thee, who shall proceed out of thy own body, and I will establish his kingdom.

column.name: text
column.value: He shall build an house for my name, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom for ever.

column.name: text
column.value: I will be his father, and he shall be my son. If he shall commit iniquity, I will chasten him with the rod of men, and with the stripes of the children of men:

column.name: text
column.value: But my mercy shall not depart from him, as I took {it} from Saul, whom I put away before thee.

column.name: text
column.value: And thy house and thy kingdom shall be established for ever before thee: thy throne shall be established for ever.

column.name: text
column.value: According to all these words, and according to all this vision, so did Nathan speak to David.

column.name: text
column.value: Then king David went in, and sat before the LORD, and he said, Who {am} I, O Lord GOD? and what {is} my house, that thou hast brought me thus far?

column.name: text
column.value: And this was yet a small thing in thy sight, O Lord GOD; but thou hast spoken also of thy servant's house for a great while to come. And {is} this the manner of man, O Lord GOD?

column.name: text
column.value: And what can David say more to thee? for thou, Lord GOD, knowest thy servant.

column.name: text
column.value: For thy word's sake, and according to thy own heart, hast thou done all these great things, to make thy servant know {them}.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore thou art great, O LORD God: for {there is} none like thee, neither {is there any} God besides thee, according to all that we have heard with our ears.

column.name: text
column.value: And what one nation in the earth {is} like thy people, {even} like Israel, whom God went to redeem for a people to himself, and to make him a name, and to do for you great things and terrible, for thy land, before thy people, whom thou didst redeem to thee from Egypt, {from} the nations and their gods?

column.name: text
column.value: For thou hast confirmed to thyself thy people Israel {to be} a people to thee for ever: and thou, LORD, art become their God.

column.name: text
column.value: And now, O LORD God, the word that thou hast spoken concerning thy servant, and concerning his house, establish {it} for ever, and do as thou hast said.

column.name: text
column.value: And let thy name be magnified for ever, saying, The LORD of hosts {is} the God over Israel: and let the house of thy servant David be established before thee.

column.name: text
column.value: For thou, O LORD of hosts, God of Israel, hast revealed to thy servant, saying, I will build thee an house: therefore hath thy servant found in his heart to pray this prayer to thee.

column.name: text
column.value: And now, O Lord GOD, thou {art} that God, and thy words are true, and thou hast promised this goodness to thy servant:

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore now let it please thee to bless the house of thy servant, that it may continue for ever before thee: for thou, O Lord GOD, hast spoken {it}: and with thy blessing let the house of thy servant be blessed for ever.

column.name: text
column.value: And after this it came to pass, that David smote the Philistines, and subdued them: and David took Methegammah out of the hand of the Philistines.

column.name: text
column.value: And he smote Moab, and measured them with a line, casting them down to the ground; even with two lines he measured to put to death, and with one full line to keep alive. And {so} the Moabites became David's servants, {and} brought gifts.

column.name: text
column.value: David smote also Hadadezer, the son of Rehob, king of Zobah, as he went to recover his border at the river Euphrates.

column.name: text
column.value: And David took from him a thousand {chariots}, and seven hundred horsemen, and twenty thousand footmen: and David hamstrung all the chariot {horses}, but reserved of them {for} an hundred chariots.

column.name: text
column.value: And when the Syrians of Damascus came to help Hadadezer king of Zobah, David slew of the Syrians two and twenty thousand men.

column.name: text
column.value: Then David put garrisons in Syria of Damascus: and the Syrians became servants to David, {and} brought gifts. And the LORD preserved David wherever he went.

column.name: text
column.value: And David took the shields of gold that were on the servants of Hadadezer, and brought them to Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: And from Betah, and from Berothai, cities of Hadadezer, king David took very much brass.

column.name: text
column.value: When Toi king of Hamath heard that David had smitten all the host of Hadadezer,

column.name: text
column.value: Then Toi sent Joram his son to king David, to greet him, and to bless him, because he had fought against Hadadezer, and smitten him: for Hadadezer had wars with Toi. And {Joram} brought with him vessels of silver, and vessels of gold, and vessels of brass:

column.name: text
column.value: Which also king David dedicated to the LORD, with the silver and gold that he had dedicated of all nations which he subdued;

column.name: text
column.value: Of Syria, and of Moab, and of the children of Ammon, and of the Philistines, and of Amalek, and of the spoil of Hadadezer, son of Rehob, king of Zobah.

column.name: text
column.value: And David made {him} a name when he returned from smiting of the Syrians in the valley of salt, {being} eighteen thousand {men}.

column.name: text
column.value: And he put garrisons in Edom; throughout all Edom he put garrisons, and all they of Edom became David's servants. And the LORD preserved David wherever he went.

column.name: text
column.value: And David reigned over all Israel; and David executed judgment and justice to all his people.

column.name: text
column.value: And Joab the son of Zeruiah {was} over the host; and Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud {was} recorder;

column.name: text
column.value: And Zadok the son of Ahitub, and Ahimelech the son of Abiathar, {were} the priests; and Seraiah {was} the scribe;

column.name: text
column.value: And Benaiah the son of Jehoiada {was over} both the Cherethites and the Pelethites; and David's sons were chief rulers.

column.name: text
column.value: And David said, Is there yet any that is left of the house of Saul, that I may show him kindness for Jonathan's sake?

column.name: text
column.value: And {there was} of the house of Saul a servant whose name {was} Ziba. And when they had called him to David, the king said to him, {Art} thou Ziba? And he said, Thy servant {is he}.

column.name: text
column.value: And the king said, {Is} there not yet any of the house of Saul, that I may show the kindness of God to him? And Ziba said to the king, Jonathan hath yet a son, {who is} lame in {his} feet.

column.name: text
column.value: And the king said to him, Where {is} he? And Ziba said to the king, Behold, he {is} in the house of Machir, the son of Ammiel, in Lodebar.

column.name: text
column.value: Then king David sent, and brought him from the house of Machir, the son of Ammiel, from Lodebar.

column.name: text
column.value: Now when Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, had come to David, he fell on his face, and did reverence. And David said, Mephibosheth. And he answered, Behold thy servant!

column.name: text
column.value: And David said to him, Fear not: for I will surely show thee kindness for the sake of Jonathan thy father, and will restore thee all the land of Saul thy father; and thou shalt eat bread at my table continually.

column.name: text
column.value: And he bowed himself, and said, What {is} thy servant, that thou shouldest look upon such a dead dog as I {am}?

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king called to Ziba, Saul's servant, and said to him, I have given to thy master's son all that pertained to Saul and to all his house.

column.name: text
column.value: Thou therefore, and thy sons, and thy servants, shall till the land for him, and thou shalt bring in {the fruits}, that thy master's son may have food to eat: but Mephibosheth thy master's son shall eat bread always at my table. Now Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants.

column.name: text
column.value: Then said Ziba to the king, According to all that my lord the king hath commanded his servant, so shall thy servant do. As for Mephibosheth, {said the king}, he shall eat at my table, as one of the king's sons.

column.name: text
column.value: And Mephibosheth had a young son, whose name {was} Micha. And all that dwelt in the house of Ziba {were} servants to Mephibosheth.

column.name: text
column.value: So Mephibosheth dwelt in Jerusalem: for he ate continually at the king's table; and was lame in both his feet.

column.name: text
column.value: And it came to pass, after the year had ended, at the time when kings go forth {to battle}, that David sent Joab, and his servants with him, and all Israel; and they destroyed the children of Ammon, and destroyed Rabbah. But David tarried still at Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: And it came to pass in an evening, that David arose from off his bed, and walked upon the roof of the king's house: and from the roof he saw a woman washing herself; and the woman {was} very beautiful to look upon.

column.name: text
column.value: And David sent and enquired after the woman. And {one} said, {Is} not this Bathsheba, the daughter of Eliam, the wife of Uriah the Hittite?

column.name: text
column.value: And David sent messengers, and took her; and she came in to him, and he lay with her; for she was purified from her uncleanness: and she returned to her house.

column.name: text
column.value: And the woman conceived, and sent and told David, and said, I {am} with child.

column.name: text
column.value: And David sent to Joab, {saying}, Send me Uriah the Hittite. And Joab sent Uriah to David.

column.name: text
column.value: And when Uriah had come to him, David enquired {of him} how Joab did, and how the people did, and how the war prospered.

column.name: text
column.value: And David said to Uriah, Go down to thy house, and wash thy feet. And Uriah departed out of the king's house, and there followed him a present from the king.

column.name: text
column.value: But Uriah slept at the door of the king's house with all the servants of his lord, and went not down to his house.

column.name: text
column.value: And when they had told David, saying, Uriah went not down to his house, David said to Uriah, Camest thou not from {thy} journey? why {then} didst thou not go down to thy house?

column.name: text
column.value: And Uriah said to David, The ark, and Israel, and Judah, abide in tents; and my lord Joab, and the servants of my lord, are encamped in the open fields; shall I then go into my house, to eat and to drink, and to lie with my wife? {as} thou livest, and {as} thy soul liveth, I will not do this thing.

column.name: text
column.value: And David said to Uriah, Tarry here to day also, and to morrow I will let thee depart. So Uriah abode in Jerusalem that day, and the next.

column.name: text
column.value: And when David had called him, he ate and drank before him; and he made him drunk: and at evening he went out to lie on his bed with the servants of his lord, but went not down to his house.

column.name: text
column.value: And it came to pass in the morning, that David wrote a letter to Joab, and sent {it} by the hand of Uriah.

column.name: text
column.value: And he wrote in the letter, saying, Set ye Uriah in the front line of the hottest battle, and retire ye from him, that he may be smitten, and die.

column.name: text
column.value: And it came to pass, when Joab observed the city, that he assigned Uriah to a place where he knew that valiant men {were}.

column.name: text
column.value: And the men of the city went out, and fought with Joab: and there fell {some} of the people of the servants of David; and Uriah the Hittite died also.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Joab sent and told David all the things concerning the war;

column.name: text
column.value: And charged the messenger, saying, When thou hast finished telling the matters of the war to the king,

column.name: text
column.value: And if the king's wrath shall rise, and he shall say to thee, Why approached ye so near to the city for the fight? knew ye not that they would shoot from the wall?

column.name: text
column.value: Who smote Abimelech the son of Jerubbesheth? did not a woman cast a piece of a millstone upon him from the wall, that he died in Thebez? why went ye near the wall? then say thou, Thy servant Uriah the Hittite is dead also.

column.name: text
column.value: So the messenger went, and came and showed David all that Joab had sent him for.

column.name: text
column.value: And the messenger said to David, Surely the men prevailed against us, and came out to us into the field, and we were upon them even to the entrance of the gate.

column.name: text
column.value: And the shooters shot from off the wall upon thy servants; and {some} of the king's servants are dead, and thy servant Uriah the Hittite is dead also.

column.name: text
column.value: Then David said to the messenger, Thus shalt thou say to Joab, Let not this thing displease thee, for the sword devoureth one as well as another: make thy battle more strong against the city, and overthrow it: and encourage thou him.

column.name: text
column.value: And when the wife of Uriah heard that Uriah her husband was dead, she mourned for her husband.

column.name: text
column.value: And when the mourning was past, David sent and brought her to his house, and she became his wife, and bore him a son. But the thing that David had done displeased the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Again, David gathered together all {the} chosen {men} of Israel, thirty thousand.

column.name: text
column.value: And David arose, and went with all the people that {were} with him from Baale of Judah, to bring up from there the ark of God, whose name is called by the name of the LORD of hosts that dwelleth {between} the cherubim.

column.name: text
column.value: And they set the ark of God upon a new cart, and brought it out of the house of Abinadab that {was} in Gibeah: and Uzzah and Ahio, the sons of Abinadab, drove the new cart.

column.name: text
column.value: And they brought it out of the house of Abinadab which {was} at Gibeah, accompanying the ark of God: and Ahio went before the ark.

column.name: text
column.value: And David and all the house of Israel played before the LORD on all manner of {instruments made of} fir wood, even on harps, and on psalteries, and on timbrels, and on cornets, and on cymbals.

column.name: text
column.value: And when they came to Nachon's threshingfloor, Uzzah put forth {his hand} to the ark of God, and took hold of it; for the oxen shook {it}.

column.name: text
column.value: And the anger of the LORD was kindled against Uzzah; and God smote him there for {his} error; and there he died by the ark of God.

column.name: text
column.value: And David was displeased, because the LORD had broken forth {in anger} against Uzzah: and he called the name of the place Perezuzzah to this day.

column.name: text
column.value: And David was afraid of the LORD that day, and said, How shall the ark of the LORD come to me?

column.name: text
column.value: So David would not remove the ark of the LORD to him into the city of David: but David carried it aside into the house of Obededom the Gittite.

column.name: text
column.value: And the ark of the LORD continued in the house of Obededom the Gittite three months: and the LORD blessed Obededom, and all his household.

column.name: text
column.value: And it was told king David, saying, The LORD hath blessed the house of Obededom, and all that {pertaineth} to him, because of the ark of God. So David went and brought up the ark of God from the house of Obededom into the city of David with gladness.

column.name: text
column.value: And it was {so}, that when they that bore the ark of the LORD had gone six paces, he sacrificed oxen and fatlings.

column.name: text
column.value: And David danced before the LORD with all {his} might; and David {was} girded with a linen ephod.

column.name: text
column.value: So David and all the house of Israel brought up the ark of the LORD with shouting, and with the sound of the trumpet.

column.name: text
column.value: And as the ark of the LORD came into the city of David, Michal Saul's daughter looked through a window, and saw king David leaping and dancing before the LORD; and she despised him in her heart.

column.name: text
column.value: And they brought in the ark of the LORD, and set it in its place, inside the tabernacle that David had pitched for it: and David offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: And as soon as David had finished offering burnt offerings and peace offerings, he blessed the people in the name of the LORD of hosts.

column.name: text
column.value: And he distributed among all the people, {even} among the whole multitude of Israel, as well to the women as men, to every one a cake of bread, and a good piece {of flesh}, and a flagon {of wine}. So all the people departed every one to his house.

column.name: text
column.value: Then David returned to bless his household. And Michal the daughter of Saul came out to meet David, and said, How glorious was the king of Israel to day, who uncovered himself to day in the eyes of the handmaids of his servants, as one of the foolish fellows shamelessly uncovereth himself!

column.name: text
column.value: And David said to Michal, {It was} before the LORD, who chose me before thy father, and before all his house, to appoint me ruler over the people of the LORD, over Israel: therefore will I play before the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: And I will yet be more contemptible than this, and will be base in my own sight: and by the maidservants which thou hast spoken of, by them shall I be had in honour.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore Michal the daughter of Saul had no child until the day of her death.

column.name: text
column.value: And it came to pass after this, that the king of the children of Ammon died, and Hanun his son reigned in his stead.

column.name: text
column.value: Then said David, I will show kindness to Hanun the son of Nahash, as his father showed kindness to me. And David sent to comfort him by the hand of his servants for his father. And David's servants came into the land of the children of Ammon.

column.name: text
column.value: And the princes of the children of Ammon said to Hanun their lord, Thinkest thou that David doth honour thy father, that he hath sent comforters to thee? hath not David {rather} sent his servants to thee, to search the city, and to spy it out, and to overthrow it?

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore Hanun took David's servants, and shaved off the one half of their beards, and cut off their garments in the middle, {even} to their buttocks, and sent them away.

column.name: text
column.value: When they told {it} to David, he sent to meet them, because the men were greatly ashamed: and the king said, Tarry at Jericho until your beards are grown, and {then} return.

column.name: text
column.value: And when the children of Ammon saw that they stank before David, the children of Ammon sent and hired the Syrians of Bethrehob, and the Syrians of Zoba, twenty thousand footmen, and of king Maacah a thousand men, and of Ishtob twelve thousand men.

column.name: text
column.value: And when David heard of {it}, he sent Joab, and all the host of the mighty men.

column.name: text
column.value: And the children of Ammon came out, and put the battle in array at the entrance of the gate: and the Syrians of Zoba, and of Rehob, and Ishtob, and Maacah, {were} by themselves in the field.

column.name: text
column.value: When Joab saw that the front of the battle was against him before and behind, he chose of all the choice {men} of Israel, and put {them} in array against the Syrians:

column.name: text
