column.value: Now when we had come in sight of Cyprus, we left it on the left hand, and sailed into Syria, and landed at Tyre: for there the ship was to unload her cargo.

column.name: text
column.value: And finding disciples, we tarried there seven days: who said to Paul through the Spirit, that he should not go up to Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: And when we had come to the end of those days, we departed and went on our way; and they all accompanied us on our way, with wives and children, till {we were} out of the city: and we kneeled down on the shore, and prayed.

column.name: text
column.value: And when we had taken our leave one of another, we took ship; and they returned home again.

column.name: text
column.value: And when we had finished {our} course from Tyre, we came to Ptolemais, and greeted the brethren, and abode with them one day.

column.name: text
column.value: And the next {day} we that were of Paul's company departed, and came to Caesarea: and we entered into the house of Philip the evangelist, who was {one} of the seven; and abode with him.

column.name: text
column.value: And the same man had four daughters, virgins, who prophesied.

column.name: text
column.value: And as we tarried {there} many days, there came down from Judaea a certain prophet, named Agabus.

column.name: text
column.value: And when he had come to us, he took Paul's belt, and bound his own hands and feet, and said, Thus saith the Holy Spirit, So shall the Jews at Jerusalem bind the man that owneth this belt, and shall deliver {him} into the hands of the Gentiles.

column.name: text
column.value: And when we heard these things, both we, and they of that place, besought him not to go up to Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Paul answered, What mean ye to weep and to break my heart? for I am ready not to be bound only, but also to die at Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.

column.name: text
column.value: And when he would not be persuaded, we ceased, saying, The will of the Lord be done.

column.name: text
column.value: And after those days we got ready, and went up to Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: There went with us also {certain} of the disciples of Caesarea, and brought with them one Mnason of Cyprus, an early disciple, with whom we should lodge.

column.name: text
column.value: And when we had come to Jerusalem, the brethren received us gladly.

column.name: text
column.value: And the {day} following Paul went in with us to James; and all the elders were present.

column.name: text
column.value: And when he had greeted them, he declared particularly what things God had wrought among the Gentiles by his ministry.

column.name: text
column.value: And when they heard {it}, they glorified the Lord, and said to him, Thou seest, brother, how many thousands of Jews there are who believe; and they are all zealous of the law:

column.name: text
column.value: And they are informed concerning thee, that thou teachest all the Jews who are among the Gentiles to forsake Moses, saying that they ought not to circumcise {their} children, neither to walk after the customs.

column.name: text
column.value: What is it therefore? the multitude must needs come together: for they will hear that thou art come.

column.name: text
column.value: Do therefore this that we say to thee: We have four men who have a vow on them;

column.name: text
column.value: Take them and purify thyself with them, and pay their expenses that they may shave {their} heads: and all may know that those things, of which they were informed concerning thee, are nothing; but {that} thou thyself also walkest orderly, and keepest the law.

column.name: text
column.value: As concerning the Gentiles who believe, we have written {and} concluded that they observe no such thing, except that they keep themselves from {things} offered to idols, and from blood, and from strangled, and from immorality.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Paul took the men, and the next day purifying himself with them entered into the temple, to signify the accomplishment of the days of purification, until an offering should be offered for every one of them.

column.name: text
column.value: And when the seven days were almost ended, the Jews who were from Asia, when they saw him in the temple, stirred up all the people, and laid hands on him,

column.name: text
column.value: Crying out, Men of Israel, help: This is the man, that teacheth all {men} every where against the people, and the law, and this place: and further hath brought Greeks also into the temple, and hath polluted this holy place.

column.name: text
column.value: (For they had seen before with him in the city Trophimus an Ephesian, whom they supposed that Paul had brought into the temple.)

column.name: text
column.value: And all the city was moved, and the people ran together: and they took Paul, and drew him out of the temple: and immediately the doors were shut.

column.name: text
column.value: And as they went about to kill him, tidings came to the chief captain of the band, that all Jerusalem was in an uproar.

column.name: text
column.value: Who immediately took soldiers and centurions, and ran down to them: and when they saw the chief captain and the soldiers, they stopped beating Paul.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the chief captain came near, and took him, and commanded {him} to be bound with two chains; and demanded who he was, and what he had done.

column.name: text
column.value: And some cried one thing, some another, among the multitude: and when he could not know the certainty for the tumult, he commanded him to be carried into the barracks.

column.name: text
column.value: And when he came upon the stairs, so it was, that he was borne by the soldiers for the violence of the people.

column.name: text
column.value: For the multitude of the people followed, crying, Away with him.

column.name: text
column.value: And as Paul was to be led into the barracks, he said to the chief captain, May I speak to thee? Who said, Canst thou speak Greek?

column.name: text
column.value: Art not thou that Egyptian, who before these days madest an uproar, and leddest out into the wilderness four thousand men that were murderers?

column.name: text
column.value: But Paul said, I am a man {who is} a Jew of Tarsus, {a city} of Cilicia, a citizen of no mean city: and, I beseech thee, permit me to speak to the people.

column.name: text
column.value: And when he had given him permission, Paul stood on the stairs, and beckoned with the hand to the people. And when there was made a great silence, he spoke to {them} in the Hebrew language, saying,

column.name: text
column.value: And Paul, earnestly beholding the council, said, Men, brethren, I have lived in all good conscience before God until this day.

column.name: text
column.value: And the high priest Ananias commanded them that stood by him to strike him on the mouth.

column.name: text
column.value: Then said Paul to him, God shall smite thee, {thou} whitewashed wall: for sittest thou to judge me according to the law, and commandest me to be smitten contrary to the law?

column.name: text
column.value: And they that stood by said, Revilest thou God's high priest?

column.name: text
column.value: Then said Paul, I knew not, brethren, that he is the high priest: for it is written, Thou shalt not speak evil of the ruler of thy people.

column.name: text
column.value: But when Paul perceived that the one part were Sadducees, and the other Pharisees, he cried out in the council, Men, brethren, I am a Pharisee, the son of a Pharisee: concerning the hope and resurrection of the dead I am called in question.

column.name: text
column.value: And when he had so said, there arose a dissension between the Pharisees and the Sadducees: and the multitude was divided.

column.name: text
column.value: For the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, neither angel, nor spirit: but the Pharisees confess both.

column.name: text
column.value: And there arose a great cry: and the scribes {that were} of the Pharisees' part arose, and contended, saying, We find no evil in this man: but if a spirit or an angel hath spoken to him, let us not fight against God.

column.name: text
column.value: And when there arose a great dissension, the chief captain, fearing lest Paul should have been pulled in pieces by them, commanded the soldiers to go down, and to take him by force from among them, and to bring {him} into the barracks.

column.name: text
column.value: And the night following the Lord stood by him, and said, Be of good cheer, Paul: for as thou hast testified concerning me in Jerusalem, so must thou bear testimony also at Rome.

column.name: text
column.value: And when it was day, certain of the Jews banded together, and bound themselves under a curse, saying that they would neither eat nor drink till they had killed Paul.

column.name: text
column.value: And they were more than forty who had made this conspiracy.

column.name: text
column.value: And they came to the chief priests and elders, and said, We have bound ourselves under a great curse, that we will eat nothing until we have slain Paul.

column.name: text
column.value: Now therefore ye with the council signify to the chief captain that he bring him down to you to morrow, as though ye would enquire something more perfectly concerning him: and we, before he shall come near, are ready to kill him.

column.name: text
column.value: And when the son of Paul's sister heard of their lying in wait, he went and entered into the barracks, and told Paul.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Paul called one of the centurions to {him}, and said, Bring this young man to the chief captain: for he hath a certain thing to tell him.

column.name: text
column.value: So he took him, and brought {him} to the chief captain, and said, Paul the prisoner called me to {him}, and asked me to bring this young man to thee, who hath something to say to thee.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the chief captain took him by the hand, and went {with him} aside privately, and asked {him}, What is that thou hast to tell me?

column.name: text
column.value: And he said, The Jews have agreed to desire thee that thou wouldest bring down Paul to morrow into the council, as though they would enquire somewhat concerning him more perfectly.

column.name: text
column.value: But do not thou yield to them: for there are of them who lie in wait for him more than forty men, who have bound themselves with an oath, that they will neither eat nor drink till they have killed him: and now they are ready, looking for a promise from thee.

column.name: text
column.value: So the chief captain {then} let the young man depart, and charged {him, See thou} tell no man that thou hast shown these things to me.

column.name: text
column.value: And he called to {him} two centurions, saying, Make ready two hundred soldiers to go to Caesarea, and seventy horsemen, and spearmen two hundred, at the third hour of the night;

column.name: text
column.value: And provide for {them} beasts, that they may set Paul on, and bring {him} safe to Felix the governor.

column.name: text
column.value: And he wrote a letter after this manner:

column.name: text
column.value: Claudius Lysias to the most excellent governor Felix {sendeth} greeting.

column.name: text
column.value: This man was taken by the Jews, and should have been killed by them: then I came with a body of soldiers, and rescued him, having understood that he was a Roman.

column.name: text
column.value: And when I would have known the cause for which they accused him, I brought him forth into their council:

column.name: text
column.value: Whom I perceived to be accused of questions of their law, but to have nothing laid to his charge worthy of death or of bonds.

column.name: text
column.value: And when it was told to me that the Jews laid wait for the man, I sent immediately to thee, and gave commandment to his accusers also to say before thee what {they had} against him. Farewell.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the soldiers, as it was commanded them, took Paul, and brought {him} by night to Antipatris.

column.name: text
column.value: On the next day they left the horsemen to go with him, and returned to the barracks:

column.name: text
column.value: Who, when they came to Caesarea, and delivered the epistle to the governor, presented Paul also before him.

column.name: text
column.value: And when the governor had read {the letter}, he asked of what province he was. And when he understood that {he was} of Cilicia;

column.name: text
column.value: I will hear thee, said he, when thy accusers also have come. And he commanded him to be kept in Herod's judgment hall.

column.name: text
column.value: And after five days Ananias the high priest descended with the elders, and {with} a certain orator {named} Tertullus, who informed the governor against Paul.

column.name: text
column.value: And when he was called forth, Tertullus began to accuse {him}, saying, Seeing that by thee we enjoy great quietness, and that very worthy deeds are done to this nation by thy providence,

column.name: text
column.value: We accept {it} always, and in all places, most noble Felix, with all thankfulness.

column.name: text
column.value: However, that I may not be further tedious to thee, I beseech thee that thou wouldest of thy clemency hear us a few words.

column.name: text
column.value: For we have found this man {a} pestilent {fellow}, and a mover of sedition among all the Jews throughout the world, and a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes:

column.name: text
column.value: Who also hath gone about to profane the temple: whom we took, and would have judged according to our law.

column.name: text
column.value: But the chief captain Lysias came, and with great violence took {him} out of our hands,

column.name: text
column.value: Commanding his accusers to come to thee: by examining whom thou thyself mayest take knowledge of all these things, of which we accuse him.

column.name: text
column.value: And the Jews also assented, saying that these things were so.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Paul, after the governor had beckoned to him to speak, answered, Forasmuch as I know that thou hast been for many years a judge to this nation, I do the more cheerfully answer for myself:

column.name: text
column.value: That thou mayest understand, that there are yet but twelve days since I went up to Jerusalem to worship.

column.name: text
column.value: And they neither found me in the temple disputing with any man, neither provoking the people to sedition, neither in the synagogues, nor in the city:

column.name: text
column.value: Neither can they prove the things of which they now accuse me.

column.name: text
column.value: But this I confess to thee, that after the way which they call heresy, so I worship the God of my fathers, believing all things which are written in the law and in the prophets:

column.name: text
column.value: And have hope toward God, which they themselves also allow, that there shall be a resurrection of the dead, both of the just and unjust.

column.name: text
column.value: And in this I exercise myself, to have always a conscience void of offence toward God, and {toward} men.

column.name: text
column.value: Now after many years I came to bring alms to my nation, and offerings.

column.name: text
column.value: Upon which certain Jews from Asia found me purified in the temple, neither with multitude, nor with tumult.

column.name: text
column.value: Who ought to have been here before thee, and object, if they had any thing against me.

column.name: text
column.value: Or else let these same {here} say, if they have found any evil doing in me, while I stood before the council,

column.name: text
column.value: Except it is for this one thing, that I cried standing among them, Concerning the resurrection of the dead I am called in question by you this day.

column.name: text
column.value: And when Felix heard these things, having more perfect knowledge of {that} way, he deferred them, and said, When Lysias the chief captain shall come down, I will make a decision on your case.

column.name: text
column.value: And he commanded a centurion to keep Paul, and to let {him} have liberty, and that he should forbid none of his acquaintance to minister or come to him.

column.name: text
column.value: And after certain days, when Felix came with his wife Drusilla, who was a Jewess, he sent for Paul, and heard him concerning the faith in Christ.

column.name: text
column.value: And as he reasoned of righteousness, self-control, and judgment to come, Felix trembled, and answered, Go thy way for this time; when I have a convenient season, I will call for thee.

column.name: text
column.value: He hoped also that money should have been given him by Paul, that he might loose him: therefore he sent for him the oftener, and communed with him.

column.name: text
column.value: But after two years Porcius Festus came in place of Felix: and Felix, willing to show the Jews a favour, left Paul bound.

column.name: text
column.value: Now when Festus had come into the province, after three days he went up from Caesarea to Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the high priest and the chief of the Jews informed him against Paul, and besought him,

column.name: text
column.value: And desired favour against him, that he would send for him to Jerusalem, laying wait in the way to kill him.

column.name: text
column.value: But Festus answered, that Paul should be kept at Caesarea, and that he himself would depart shortly {there}.

column.name: text
column.value: Let them therefore, said he, who among you are able, go down with {me}, and accuse this man, if there is any wickedness in him.

column.name: text
column.value: And when he had tarried among them more than ten days, he went down to Caesarea; and the next day sitting on the judgment seat commanded Paul to be brought.

column.name: text
column.value: And when he had come, the Jews who came down from Jerusalem stood around, and laid many and grievous complaints against Paul, which they could not prove.

column.name: text
column.value: While he answered for himself, Neither against the law of the Jews, neither against the temple, nor yet against Caesar, have I committed any offence.

column.name: text
column.value: But Festus, willing to do the Jews a favour, answered Paul, and said, Wilt thou go to Jerusalem, and there be judged concerning these things before me?

column.name: text
column.value: Then said Paul, I stand at Caesar's judgment seat, where I ought to be judged: to the Jews have I done no wrong, as thou very well knowest.

column.name: text
column.value: For if I am an offender, or have committed any thing worthy of death, I refuse not to die: but if there is none of these things of which these accuse me, no man may deliver me to them. I appeal to Caesar.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Festus, when he had conferred with the council, answered, Hast thou appealed to Caesar? to Caesar thou shalt go.

column.name: text
column.value: And after certain days king Agrippa and Bernice came to Caesarea to greet Festus.

column.name: text
column.value: And when they had been there many days, Festus declared Paul's cause to the king, saying, There is a certain man left in bonds by Felix:

column.name: text
column.value: About whom, when I was at Jerusalem, the chief priests and the elders of the Jews informed {me}, desiring {to have} judgment against him.

column.name: text
column.value: To whom I answered, It is not the manner of the Romans to deliver any man to die, before he who is accused hath the accusers face to face, and hath opportunity to answer for himself concerning the charge laid against him.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore, when they had come here, without any delay on the next day I sat on the judgment seat, and commanded the man to be brought forth.

column.name: text
column.value: Against whom when the accusers stood up, they brought no accusation of such things as I supposed:

column.name: text
column.value: But had certain questions against him of their own religion, and of one Jesus, who was dead, whom Paul affirmed to be alive.

column.name: text
column.value: And because I was perplexed concerning such manner of questions, I asked {him} whether he would go to Jerusalem, and there be judged concerning these matters.

column.name: text
column.value: But when Paul had appealed to be reserved to the hearing of Augustus, I commanded him to be kept till I might send him to Caesar.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Agrippa said to Festus, I would also hear the man myself. To morrow, said he, thou shalt hear him.

column.name: text
column.value: And on the next day, when Agrippa had come, and Bernice, with great pomp, and had entered into the place of hearing, with the chief captains, and principal men of the city, at the command of Festus Paul was brought forth.

column.name: text
column.value: And Festus said, King Agrippa, and all men who are here present with us, ye see this man, about whom all the multitude of the Jews have dealt with me, both at Jerusalem, and {also} here, crying that he ought not to live any longer.

column.name: text
column.value: But when I found that he had committed nothing worthy of death, and that he himself hath appealed to Augustus, I have determined to send him.

column.name: text
column.value: Of whom I have no certain thing to write to my lord. Therefore I have brought him forth before you, and especially before thee, O king Agrippa, that, after examination had, I may have somewhat to write.

column.name: text
column.value: For it seemeth to me unreasonable to send a prisoner, and not also to signify the charges {laid} against him.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Agrippa said to Paul, Thou art permitted to speak for thyself. Then Paul stretched forth the hand, and answered for himself:

column.name: text
column.value: I think myself happy, king Agrippa, because I shall answer for myself this day before thee concerning all the things of which I am accused by the Jews:

column.name: text
column.value: Especially {because I know } thee to be expert in all customs and questions which are among the Jews: therefore I beseech thee to hear me patiently.

column.name: text
column.value: My manner of life from my youth, which was at the first among my own nation at Jerusalem, know all the Jews;

column.name: text
column.value: Who knew me from the beginning, if they would testify, that after the most strict sect of our religion I lived a Pharisee.

column.name: text
column.value: And now I stand and am judged for the hope of the promise made by God to our fathers:

column.name: text
column.value: To which {promise} our twelve tribes, earnestly serving {God} day and night, hope to come. For which hope's sake, king Agrippa, I am accused by the Jews.

column.name: text
column.value: Why should it be thought a thing incredible with you, that God should raise the dead?

column.name: text
column.value: I verily thought with myself, that I ought to do many things contrary to the name of Jesus of Nazareth.

column.name: text
column.value: Which thing I also did in Jerusalem: and many of the saints did I shut up in prison, having received authority from the chief priests; and when they were put to death, I gave my voice against {them}.

column.name: text
column.value: And I punished them often in every synagogue, and compelled {them} to blaspheme; and being exceedingly mad against them, I persecuted {them} even to foreign cities.

column.name: text
column.value: Upon which as I went to Damascus with authority and commission from the chief priests,

column.name: text
column.value: At noon, O king, I saw in the way a light from heaven, beyond the brightness of the sun, shining around me and them who journeyed with me.

column.name: text
column.value: And when we had all fallen to the earth, I heard a voice speaking to me, and saying in the Hebrew language, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me? {it is} hard for thee to kick against the goads.

column.name: text
column.value: And I said, Who art thou, Lord? And he said, I am Jesus whom thou persecutest.

column.name: text
column.value: But rise, and stand upon thy feet: for I have appeared to thee for this purpose, to make thee a minister and a witness both of the things which thou hast seen, and of the things in which I will appear to thee;

column.name: text
column.value: Delivering thee from the people, and {from} the Gentiles, to whom now I send thee,

column.name: text
column.value: To open their eyes, {and} to turn {them} from darkness to light, and {from} the power of Satan to God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins, and inheritance among them who are sanctified by faith that is in me.

column.name: text
column.value: Upon which, O king Agrippa, I was not disobedient to the heavenly vision:

column.name: text
column.value: But showed first to them of Damascus, and at Jerusalem, and throughout all the region of Judaea, and {then} to the Gentiles, that they should repent and turn to God, and do works fit for repentance.

column.name: text
column.value: For these causes the Jews caught me in the temple, and went about to kill {me}.

column.name: text
column.value: Having therefore obtained help from God, I continue to this day, witnessing both to small and great, saying no other things than those which the prophets and Moses did say should come:

column.name: text
column.value: That Christ should suffer, {and} that he should be the first that should rise from the dead, and should show light to the people, and to the Gentiles.

column.name: text
column.value: And as he was thus speaking for himself, Festus said with a loud voice, Paul, thou art beside thyself; much learning doth make thee mad.

column.name: text
column.value: But he said, I am not mad, most noble Festus; but speak forth the words of truth and soberness.

column.name: text
column.value: For the king knoweth of these things, before whom also I speak freely: for I am persuaded that none of these things are hidden from him; for this thing was not done in a corner.

column.name: text
column.value: King Agrippa, believest thou the prophets? I know that thou believest.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Agrippa said to Paul, Almost thou persuadest me to be a Christian.

column.name: text
column.value: And Paul said, I would to God, that not only thou, but also all that hear me this day, were both almost, and altogether such as I am, except these bonds.

column.name: text
column.value: And when he had thus spoken, the king rose, and the governor, and Bernice, and they that sat with them:

column.name: text
column.value: And when they had gone aside, they talked between themselves, saying, This man doeth nothing worthy of death or of bonds.

column.name: text
column.value: Then said Agrippa to Festus, This man might have been set at liberty, if he had not appealed to Caesar.

column.name: text
column.value: And when it was determined that we should sail into Italy, they delivered Paul and certain other prisoners to {one} named Julius, a centurion of Augustus' band.

column.name: text
column.value: And entering into a ship of Adramyttium, we launched, meaning to sail by the coasts of Asia; {one} Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, being with us.

column.name: text
column.value: And the next {day} we touched at Sidon. And Julius courteously treated Paul, and gave {him} liberty to go to his friends to refresh himself.

column.name: text
column.value: And when we had launched from there, we sailed under Cyprus, because the winds were contrary.

column.name: text
column.value: And when we had sailed over the sea of Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra, {a city} of Lycia.

column.name: text
column.value: And there the centurion found a ship of Alexandria sailing into Italy; and he put us on board.

column.name: text
column.value: And when we had sailed slowly many days, and scarce had come off Cnidus, the wind did not permit us, we sailed under Crete, off Salmone;

column.name: text
column.value: And, scarcely passing it, came to a place which is called The fair havens; near which was the city {of} Lasea.

column.name: text
column.value: Now when much time was spent, and when sailing was now dangerous, because the fast was now already past, Paul admonished {them},

column.name: text
column.value: And said to them, Sirs, I perceive that this voyage will be with harm and much damage, not only of the cargo and ship, but also of our lives.

column.name: text
column.value: Nevertheless the centurion believed the master and the owner of the ship, more than the things which were spoken by Paul.

column.name: text
column.value: And because the haven was not suitable to winter in, the greater part advised to depart from there also, if by any means they might attain to Phenice, {and there} to winter; {which is} an haven of Crete, and lieth toward the south west and north west.

column.name: text
column.value: And when the south wind blew softly, supposing that they had obtained {their} purpose, loosing {from there}, they sailed close by Crete.

column.name: text
column.value: But not long after there arose against it a tempestuous wind, called Euroclydon.

column.name: text
column.value: And when the ship was caught, and could not bear up into the wind, we let {her} drive.

column.name: text
column.value: And running under a certain isle which is called Clauda, we had much work to secure the boat:

column.name: text
column.value: Which when they had taken {it} up, they used cables, undergirding the ship; and, fearing lest they should fall into the quicksands, struck sail, and so were driven.

column.name: text
column.value: And we being exceedingly tossed with a tempest, the next {day} they lightened the ship;

column.name: text
column.value: And the third {day} we cast out with our own hands the tackling of the ship.

column.name: text
column.value: And when neither sun nor stars in many days appeared, and no small tempest lay on {us}, all hope that we should be saved was then taken away.

column.name: text
column.value: But after being long without food Paul stood forth in the midst of them, and said, Sirs, ye should have hearkened to me, and not have loosed from Crete, and to have gained this harm and loss.

column.name: text
column.value: And now I exhort you to be of good cheer: for there shall be no loss of life among you, but of the ship.

column.name: text
column.value: For there stood by me this night the angel of God, whose I am, and whom I serve,

column.name: text
column.value: Saying, Fear not, Paul; thou must be brought before Caesar: and, lo, God hath given thee all them that sail with thee.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore, sirs, be of good cheer: for I believe God, that it shall be even as it was told to me.

column.name: text
column.value: But we must be cast upon a certain isle.

column.name: text
column.value: But when the fourteenth night was come, as we were driven up and down in Adria, about midnight the shipmen thought that they drew near to some country;

column.name: text
column.value: And sounded, and found {it} twenty fathoms: and when they had gone a little further, they sounded again, and found {it} fifteen fathoms.

column.name: text
column.value: Then fearing lest we should fall upon rocks, they cast four anchors out of the stern, and wished for the day.

column.name: text
column.value: And as the shipmen were about to flee out of the ship, when they had let down the boat into the sea, under pretence as though they would cast anchors out of the foreship,

column.name: text
column.value: Paul said to the centurion and to the soldiers, Except these abide in the ship, ye cannot be saved.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the soldiers cut off the ropes of the boat, and let her fall off.

column.name: text
column.value: And while the day was coming on, Paul besought {them} all to take food, saying, This day is the fourteenth day that ye have tarried and continued fasting, having taken nothing.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore I beseech you to take {some} food: for this is for your health: for there shall not an hair fall from the head of any of you.

column.name: text
column.value: And when he had thus spoken, he took bread, and gave thanks to God in presence of them all: and when he had broken {it}, he began to eat.

column.name: text
column.value: Then they were all of good cheer, and they also took food.

column.name: text
column.value: And we were in all in the ship two hundred and seventy and six souls.

column.name: text
column.value: And when they had eaten enough, they lightened the ship, and cast the wheat into the sea.

column.name: text
column.value: And when it was day, they knew not the land: but they discovered a certain creek with a shore, into which they purposed, if it were possible, to thrust in the ship.

column.name: text
column.value: And when they had taken up the anchors, they committed {themselves} to the sea, and loosed the rudder bands, and hoisted the mainsail to the wind, and made toward the shore.

column.name: text
column.value: And falling into a place where two seas met, they ran the ship aground; and the bow stuck fast, and remained unmoveable, but the stern was broken with the violence of the waves.

column.name: text
column.value: And the soldiers' counsel was to kill the prisoners, lest any of them should swim out, and escape.

column.name: text
column.value: But the centurion, willing to save Paul, kept them from {their} purpose; and commanded that they who could swim should cast {themselves} first {into the sea}, and get to land:

column.name: text
column.value: And the rest, some on boards, and some on {broken pieces} of the ship. And so it came to pass, that they all escaped safe to land.

column.name: text
column.value: Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, called {to be} an apostle, separated to the gospel of God,

column.name: text
column.value: (Which he had promised before by his prophets in the holy scriptures,)

column.name: text
column.value: Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, who was born of the seed of David according to the flesh;

column.name: text
column.value: And declared {to be} the Son of God with power, according to the spirit of holiness, by the resurrection from the dead:

column.name: text
column.value: By whom we have received grace and apostleship, for obedience to the faith among all nations, for his name:

column.name: text
column.value: Among whom are ye also the called of Jesus Christ:

column.name: text
column.value: To all that are in Rome, beloved of God, called {to be} saints: Grace to you and peace from God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ.

column.name: text
column.value: First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for you all, that your faith is spoken of throughout the whole world.

column.name: text
column.value: For God is my witness, whom I serve with my spirit in the gospel of his Son, that without ceasing I make mention of you always in my prayers;

column.name: text
column.value: Making request, if by any means now at length I may have a prosperous journey by the will of God to come to you.

column.name: text
column.value: For I long to see you, that I may impart to you some spiritual gift, to the end {that} ye may be established;

column.name: text
column.value: That is, that I may be comforted together with you by the mutual faith both of you and me.

column.name: text
column.value: Now I would not have you ignorant, brethren, that I have often purposed to come to you, (but was hindered until now,) that I might have some fruit among you also, even as among other Gentiles.

column.name: text
column.value: I am debtor both to the Greeks, and to the Barbarians; both to the wise, and to the unwise.

column.name: text
column.value: So, as much as in me is, I am ready to preach the gospel to you that are at Rome also.

column.name: text
column.value: For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God to salvation to every one that believeth; to the Jew first, and also to the Greek.

column.name: text
column.value: For in this is the righteousness of God revealed from faith to faith: as it is written, The just shall live by faith.

column.name: text
column.value: For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness;

column.name: text
column.value: Because that which may be known of God is evident in them; for God hath shown {it} to them.

column.name: text
column.value: For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, {even} his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse:

column.name: text
column.value: Because that, when they knew God, they glorified {him} not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened.

column.name: text
column.value: Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools,

column.name: text
column.value: And changed the glory of the incorruptible God into an image made like corruptible man, and birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves:

column.name: text
column.value: Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen.

column.name: text
column.value: For this cause God gave them up to vile affections: for even their women changed the natural use into that which is against nature:

column.name: text
column.value: And likewise also the men, leaving the natural use of the woman, burned in their lust one toward another; men with men working that which is unseemly, and receiving in themselves that recompence of their error which was due.

column.name: text
column.value: And even as they did not like to retain God in {their} knowledge, God gave them over to a debased mind, to do those things which are not proper;

column.name: text
column.value: Being filled with all unrighteousness, immorality, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, strife, deceit, malignity; whisperers,

column.name: text
column.value: Backbiters, haters of God, insolent, proud, boasters, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents,

column.name: text
column.value: Without understanding, covenantbreakers, without natural affection, implacable, unmerciful:

column.name: text
column.value: Who knowing the judgment of God, that they who commit such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but have pleasure in them that do them.

column.name: text
column.value: What advantage then hath the Jew? or what profit {is there} of circumcision?

column.name: text
column.value: Much every way: chiefly, because that to them were committed the oracles of God.

column.name: text
column.value: For what if some did not believe? shall their unbelief make the faithfulness of God without effect?

column.name: text
column.value: By no means: verily, let God be true, but every man a liar; as it is written, That thou mayest be justified in thy sayings, and mayest overcome when thou art judged.

column.name: text
column.value: But if our unrighteousness commendeth the righteousness of God, what shall we say? {Is} God unrighteous who taketh vengeance? (I speak as a man )

column.name: text
column.value: By no means: for then how shall God judge the world?

column.name: text
column.value: For if the truth of God hath more abounded through my lie to his glory; why yet am I also judged as a sinner?

column.name: text
column.value: And not {rather}, (as we are slanderously reported, and as some affirm that we say,) Let us do evil, that good may come? whose condemnation is just.

column.name: text
column.value: What then? are we better {than they}? No, in no way: for we have before proved both Jews and Gentiles, that they are all under sin;

column.name: text
column.value: As it is written, There is none righteous, no, not one:

column.name: text
column.value: There is none that understandeth, there is none that seeketh God.

column.name: text
column.value: They are all gone out of the way, they are together become unprofitable; there is none that doeth good, no, not one.

column.name: text
column.value: Their throat {is} an open sepulchre; with their tongues they have used deceit; the poison of asps {is} under their lips:

column.name: text
column.value: Whose mouth {is} full of cursing and bitterness:

column.name: text
column.value: Their feet {are} swift to shed blood:

column.name: text
column.value: Destruction and misery {are} in their ways:

column.name: text
column.value: And the way of peace have they not known:

column.name: text
column.value: There is no fear of God before their eyes.

column.name: text
column.value: Now we know that whatever the law saith, it saith to them who are under the law: that every mouth may be stopped, and all the world may become guilty before God.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore by the deeds of the law there shall no flesh be justified in his sight: for by the law {is} the knowledge of sin.

column.name: text
column.value: But now the righteousness of God apart from the law is revealed, being witnessed by the law and the prophets;

column.name: text
column.value: Even the righteousness of God {which is} by faith of Jesus Christ to all and upon all them that believe: for there is no difference:

column.name: text
column.value: For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God;

column.name: text
column.value: Being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Jesus Christ:

column.name: text
column.value: Whom God hath set forth {to be} a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past, through the forbearance of God;

column.name: text
column.value: To declare, {I say}, at this time his righteousness: that he may be just, and the justifier of him who believeth in Jesus.

column.name: text
column.value: Where {is} boasting then? It is excluded. By what law? of works? Nay: but by the law of faith.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore we conclude that a man is justified by faith apart from the deeds of the law.

column.name: text
column.value: {Is he} the God of the Jews only? {is he} not also of the Gentiles? Yes, of the Gentiles also:

column.name: text
column.value: Seeing {it is} one God, who shall justify the circumcision by faith, and uncircumcision through faith.

column.name: text
column.value: Do we then make void the law through faith? By no means: but, we establish the law.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore thou art inexcusable, O man, whoever thou art that judgest: for in that thou judgest another, thou condemnest thyself; for thou that judgest doest the same things.

column.name: text
column.value: But we are sure that the judgment of God is according to truth against them who commit such things.

column.name: text
column.value: And thinkest thou this, O man, that judgest them who do such things, and doest the same, that thou shalt escape the judgment of God?

column.name: text
column.value: Or despisest thou the riches of his goodness and forbearance and longsuffering; not knowing that the goodness of God leadeth thee to repentance?

column.name: text
column.value: But after thy hardness and impenitent heart treasurest up to thyself wrath in the day of wrath and revelation of the righteous judgment of God;

column.name: text
column.value: Who will render to every man according to his deeds:

column.name: text
column.value: To them who by patient continuance in well doing seek for glory and honour and immortality, eternal life:

column.name: text
column.value: But to them that are contentious, and do not obey the truth, but obey unrighteousness, indignation and wrath,

column.name: text
column.value: Tribulation and anguish, upon every soul of man that doeth evil, of the Jew first, and also of the Gentile;

column.name: text
column.value: But glory, honour, and peace, to every man that worketh good, to the Jew first, and also to the Gentile:

column.name: text
column.value: For there is no respect of persons with God.

column.name: text
column.value: For as many as have sinned without law shall also perish without law: and as many as have sinned in the law shall be judged by the law;

column.name: text
column.value: (For not the hearers of the law {are} just before God, but the doers of the law shall be justified.

column.name: text
column.value: For when the Gentiles, who have not the law, do by nature the things contained in the law, these, having not the law, are a law to themselves:

column.name: text
column.value: Who show the work of the law written in their hearts, their conscience also bearing witness, and {their} thoughts the mean while accusing or else excusing one another;)

column.name: text
column.value: In the day when God shall judge the secrets of men by Jesus Christ according to my gospel.

column.name: text
column.value: But if, thou art called a Jew, and restest in the law, and makest thy boast of God,

column.name: text
column.value: And knowest {his} will, and approvest the things that are more excellent, being instructed out of the law;

column.name: text
column.value: And art confident that thou thyself art a guide of the blind, a light of them who are in darkness,

column.name: text
column.value: An instructor of the foolish, a teacher of babes, who hast the form of knowledge and of the truth in the law.

column.name: text
column.value: Thou therefore who teachest another, teachest thou not thyself? thou that preachest a man should not steal, dost thou steal?

column.name: text
column.value: Thou that sayest a man should not commit adultery, dost thou commit adultery? thou that abhorrest idols, dost thou commit sacrilege?

column.name: text
column.value: Thou that makest thy boast of the law, through breaking the law dishonourest thou God?

column.name: text
column.value: For the name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles through you, as it is written.

column.name: text
column.value: For circumcision verily profiteth, if thou keepest the law: but if thou art a breaker of the law, thy circumcision is made uncircumcision.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore if the uncircumcision keepeth the righteousness of the law, shall not his uncircumcision be counted for circumcision?

column.name: text
column.value: And shall not uncircumcision which is by nature, if it keepeth the law, judge thee, who by the letter and circumcision dost transgress the law?

column.name: text
column.value: For he is not a Jew, who is one outwardly; neither {is that} circumcision, which is outward in the flesh:

column.name: text
column.value: But he {is} a Jew, who is one inwardly; and circumcision {is that} of the heart, in the spirit, {and} not in the letter; whose praise {is} not from men, but from God.

column.name: text
column.value: And when they had escaped, then they knew that the isle was called Melita.

column.name: text
column.value: And the barbarous people showed us no little kindness: for they kindled a fire, and received us every one, because of the present rain, and because of the cold.

column.name: text
column.value: And when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks, and laid {them} on the fire, there came a viper out of the heat, and fastened on his hand.

column.name: text
column.value: And when the barbarians saw the {venomous} creature hanging from his hand, they said among themselves, No doubt this man is a murderer, whom, though he hath escaped the sea, yet Vengeance alloweth not to live.

column.name: text
column.value: And he shook off the creature into the fire, and felt no harm.

column.name: text
column.value: Yet they looked when he should have swollen, or fallen down dead suddenly: but after they had looked a great while, and saw no harm come to him, they changed their minds, and said that he was a god.

column.name: text
column.value: In the same quarters were possessions of the chief man of the isle, whose name was Publius; who received us, and lodged us three days courteously.

column.name: text
column.value: And it came to pass, that the father of Publius lay sick with a fever and a bloody flux: to whom Paul entered in, and prayed, and laid his hands on him, and healed him.

column.name: text
column.value: So when this was done, others also, who had diseases in the isle, came, and were healed:

column.name: text
column.value: Who also honoured us with many honours; and when we departed, they supplied {us} with such things as were necessary.

column.name: text
column.value: And after three months we departed in a ship of Alexandria, which had wintered in the isle, whose sign was Castor and Pollux.

column.name: text
column.value: And landing at Syracuse, we tarried {there} three days.

column.name: text
column.value: And from there we sailed around, and came to Rhegium: and after one day the south wind blew, and we came the next day to Puteoli:

column.name: text
column.value: Where we found brethren, and were desired to tarry with them seven days: and so we went toward Rome.

column.name: text
column.value: And from there, when the brethren heard of us, they came to meet us as far as Appii forum, and The three taverns: whom when Paul saw, he thanked God, and took courage.

column.name: text
column.value: And when we came to Rome, the centurion delivered the prisoners to the captain of the guard: but Paul was permitted to dwell by himself with a soldier that kept him.

column.name: text
column.value: And it came to pass, that after three days Paul called together the chief of the Jews: and when they were assembled, he said to them, Men, brethren, though I have committed nothing against the people, or customs of our fathers, yet I was delivered prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans.

column.name: text
column.value: Who, when they had examined me, would have let {me} go, because there was no cause of death in me.

column.name: text
column.value: But when the Jews spoke against {it}, I was constrained to appeal to Caesar; not that I had any thing to accuse my nation of.

column.name: text
column.value: For this cause therefore have I called for you, to see {you}, and to speak with {you}: because that for the hope of Israel I am bound with this chain.

column.name: text
column.value: And they said to him, We have neither received letters from Judaea concerning thee, neither have any of the brethren that came shown or spoken any harm of thee.

column.name: text
column.value: But we desire to hear from thee what thou thinkest: for as concerning this sect, we know that every where it is spoken against.

column.name: text
column.value: And when they had appointed him a day, there came many to him into {his} lodging; to whom he expounded and testified the kingdom of God, persuading them concerning Jesus, both out of the law of Moses, and {out of} the prophets, from morning till evening.

column.name: text
column.value: And some believed the things which were spoken, and some believed not.

column.name: text
column.value: And when they agreed not among themselves, they departed, after Paul had spoken one word, Well spoke the Holy Spirit by Isaiah the prophet to our fathers,

column.name: text
column.value: Saying, Go to this people, and say, Hearing ye shall hear, and shall not understand; and seeing ye shall see, and not perceive:

column.name: text
column.value: For the heart of this people has become dull, and their ears are hard of hearing, and their eyes have they closed; lest they should see with {their} eyes, and hear with {their} ears, and understand with {their} heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them.

column.name: text
column.value: Be it known therefore to you, that the salvation of God is sent to the Gentiles, and they will hear it.

column.name: text
column.value: And when he had said these words, the Jews departed, and had great dispute among themselves.

column.name: text
column.value: And Paul dwelt two whole years in his own hired house, and received all that came in to him,

column.name: text
column.value: Preaching the kingdom of God, and teaching those things which concern the Lord Jesus Christ, with all confidence, no man forbidding him.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ:

column.name: text
column.value: By whom also we have access by faith into this grace in which we stand, and rejoice in hope of the glory of God.

column.name: text
column.value: And not only {so}, but we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience;

column.name: text
column.value: And patience, experience; and experience, hope:

column.name: text
column.value: And hope maketh not ashamed; because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Spirit who is given to us.

column.name: text
column.value: For when we were yet without strength, in due time Christ died for the ungodly.

column.name: text
column.value: For scarcely for a righteous man will one die: yet perhaps for a good man some would even dare to die.

column.name: text
column.value: But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.

column.name: text
column.value: Much more then, being now justified by his blood, we shall be saved from wrath through him.

column.name: text
column.value: For if, when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son, much more, being reconciled, we shall be saved by his life.

column.name: text
column.value: And not only {so}, but we also joy in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom we have now received the reconciliation.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore, as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned:

column.name: text
column.value: (For until the law sin was in the world: but sin is not imputed when there is no law.

column.name: text
column.value: Nevertheless death reigned from Adam to Moses, even over them that had not sinned after the similitude of Adam's transgression, who is the figure of him that was to come.

column.name: text
column.value: But not as the offence, so also {is} the free gift. For if through the offence of one many are dead, much more the grace of God, and the gift by grace, {which is } by one man, Jesus Christ, hath abounded to many.

column.name: text
column.value: And not as {it was} by one that sinned, {so is} the gift: for the judgment {was} by one to condemnation, but the free gift {is} of many offences to justification.

column.name: text
column.value: For if by one man's offence death reigned by one; much more they who receive abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness shall reign in life by one, Jesus Christ.)

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore as by the offence of one {judgment came} upon all men to condemnation; even so by the righteousness of one {the free gift came} upon all men to justification of life.

column.name: text
column.value: For as by one man's disobedience many were made sinners, so by the obedience of one shall many be made righteous.

column.name: text
column.value: Moreover the law entered, that the offence might abound. But where sin abounded, grace did much more abound:

column.name: text
column.value: That as sin hath reigned to death, even so might grace reign through righteousness to eternal life by Jesus Christ our Lord.

column.name: text
column.value: What shall we say then? Shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound?

column.name: text
column.value: By no means. How shall we, that are dead to sin, live any longer in it?

column.name: text
column.value: Know ye not, that so many of us as were baptized into Jesus Christ were baptized into his death?

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore we are buried with him by baptism into death: that as Christ was raised from the dead by the glory of the Father, even so we also should walk in newness of life.

column.name: text
column.value: For if we have been planted together in the likeness of his death, we shall be also {in the likeness} of {his} resurrection:

column.name: text
column.value: Knowing this, that our old man is crucified with {him}, that the body of sin may be destroyed, that henceforth we should not serve sin.

column.name: text
column.value: For he that is dead is freed from sin.

column.name: text
column.value: Now if we are dead with Christ, we believe that we shall also live with him:

column.name: text
column.value: Knowing that Christ being raised from the dead dieth no more; death hath no more dominion over him.

column.name: text
column.value: For in that he died, he died to sin once: but in that he liveth, he liveth to God.

column.name: text
column.value: Likewise reckon ye also yourselves to be dead indeed to sin, but alive to God through Jesus Christ our Lord.

column.name: text
column.value: Let not sin therefore reign in your mortal body, that ye should obey it in its lusts.

column.name: text
column.value: Neither yield ye your members {as} instruments of unrighteousness to sin: but yield yourselves to God, as those that are alive from the dead, and your members {as} instruments of righteousness to God.

column.name: text
column.value: For sin shall not have dominion over you: for ye are not under the law, but under grace.

column.name: text
column.value: What then? shall we sin, because we are not under the law, but under grace? By no means.

column.name: text
column.value: Know ye not, that to whom ye yield yourselves servants in obedience, his servants ye are whom ye obey; whether of sin to death, or of obedience to righteousness?

column.name: text
column.value: But God be thanked, that ye were the servants of sin, but ye have obeyed from the heart that form of doctrine which was delivered to you.

column.name: text
column.value: Being then made free from sin, ye became the servants of righteousness.

column.name: text
column.value: I speak after the manner of men because of the infirmity of your flesh: for as ye have yielded your members servants to uncleanness and to iniquity to {work} iniquity; even so now yield your members servants to righteousness to {work} holiness.

column.name: text
column.value: For when ye were the servants of sin, ye were free from righteousness.

column.name: text
column.value: What fruit had ye then in those things of which ye are now ashamed? for the end of those things {is} death.

column.name: text
column.value: But now being made free from sin, and having become servants to God, ye have your fruit to holiness, and the end everlasting life.

column.name: text
column.value: For the wages of sin {is} death; but the gift of God {is} eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.

column.name: text
column.value: What shall we then say that Abraham our father, as pertaining to the flesh, hath found?

column.name: text
column.value: For if Abraham were justified by works, he hath {something} to glory {about}; but not before God.

column.name: text
column.value: For what saith the scripture? Abraham believed God, and it was counted to him for righteousness.

column.name: text
column.value: Now to him that worketh is the reward not reckoned of grace, but of debt.

column.name: text
column.value: But to him that worketh not, but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness.

column.name: text
column.value: Even as David also describeth the blessedness of the man, to whom God imputeth righteousness apart from works,

column.name: text
column.value: {Saying}, Blessed {are} they whose iniquities are forgiven, and whose sins are covered.

column.name: text
column.value: Blessed {is} the man to whom the Lord will not impute sin.

column.name: text
column.value: {Cometh} this blessedness then upon the circumcision {only}, or upon the uncircumcision also? for we say that faith was reckoned to Abraham for righteousness.

column.name: text
column.value: How then was it reckoned? when he was in circumcision, or in uncircumcision? Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision.

column.name: text
column.value: And he received the sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of the faith which {he had yet} being uncircumcised: that he might be the father of all them that believe, though they are not circumcised; that righteousness might be imputed to them also:

column.name: text
column.value: And the father of circumcision to them who are not of the circumcision only, but who also walk in the steps of that faith of our father Abraham, which {he had} being {yet} uncircumcised.

column.name: text
column.value: For the promise, that he should be the heir of the world, {was} not to Abraham, or to his seed, through the law, but through the righteousness of faith.

column.name: text
column.value: For if they who are of the law {are} heirs, faith is made void, and the promise made of no effect:

column.name: text
column.value: Because the law worketh wrath: for where no law is, {there is} no transgression.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore {it is} of faith, that {it might be} by grace; to the end the promise might be sure to all the seed; not to that only which is of the law, but to that also which is of the faith of Abraham; who is the father of us all,

column.name: text
column.value: (As it is written, I have made thee a father of many nations,) before him whom he believed, {even} God, who giveth life to the dead, and calleth those things which are not as though they were.

column.name: text
column.value: Who against hope believed with hope, that he should become the father of many nations, according to that which was spoken, So shall thy seed be.

column.name: text
column.value: And being not weak in faith, he considered not his own body now dead, when he was about an hundred years old, neither yet the deadness of Sarah's womb:

column.name: text
column.value: He staggered not at the promise of God through unbelief; but was strong in faith, giving glory to God;

column.name: text
column.value: And being fully persuaded that, what he had promised, he was able also to perform.

column.name: text
column.value: And therefore it was imputed to him for righteousness.

column.name: text
column.value: Now it was not written for his sake alone, that it was imputed to him;

column.name: text
column.value: But for us also, to whom it shall be imputed, if we believe on him that raised Jesus our Lord from the dead;

column.name: text
column.value: Who was delivered for our offences, and raised again for our justification.

column.name: text
column.value: Know ye not, brethren, (for I speak to them that know the law,) that the law hath dominion over a man as long as he liveth?

column.name: text
column.value: For the woman who hath an husband is bound by the law to {her} husband so long as he liveth; but if the husband is dead, she is loosed from the law of {her} husband.

column.name: text
column.value: So then if, while {her} husband liveth, she is married to another man, she shall be called an adulteress: but if her husband is dead, she is free from that law; so that she is no adulteress, though she be married to another man.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore, my brethren, ye also are become dead to the law by the body of Christ; that ye should be married to another, {even} to him who is raised from the dead, that we should bring forth fruit to God.

column.name: text
column.value: For when we were in the flesh, the sinful passions, which were by the law, did work in our members to bring forth fruit to death.

column.name: text
column.value: But now we are delivered from the law, that being dead by which we were held; that we should serve in newness of spirit, and not {in} the oldness of the letter.

column.name: text
column.value: What shall we say then? {Is} the law sin? By no means. Nay, I had not known sin, but by the law: for I had not known lust, except the law had said, Thou shalt not covet.

column.name: text
column.value: But sin, taking occasion by the commandment, wrought in me all manner of lust. For apart from the law sin {was} dead.

column.name: text
column.value: For I was alive apart from the law once: but when the commandment came, sin revived, and I died.

column.name: text
column.value: And the commandment, which {was ordained} to life, I found {to be} to death.

column.name: text
column.value: For sin, taking occasion by the commandment, deceived me, and by it slew {me}.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore the law {is} holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good.

column.name: text
column.value: Was then that which is good made death to me? By no means. But sin, that it might appear sin, working death in me by that which is good; that sin by the commandment might become exceeding sinful.

column.name: text
column.value: For we know that the law is spiritual: but I am carnal, sold under sin.

column.name: text
column.value: For that which I do I understand not: for what I would, that I do not; but what I hate, that I do.

column.name: text
column.value: If then I do that which I would not, I consent to the law that {it is} good.

column.name: text
column.value: Now then it is no more I that do it, but sin that dwelleth in me.

column.name: text
column.value: For I know that in me (that is, in my flesh,) dwelleth no good thing: for to will is present with me; but {how} to perform that which is good I find not.

column.name: text
column.value: For the good that I would I do not: but the evil which I would not, that I do.

column.name: text
column.value: Now if I do that which I would not, it is no more I that do it, but sin that dwelleth in me.

column.name: text
column.value: I find then a law, that, when I would do good, evil is present with me.

column.name: text
column.value: For I delight in the law of God after the inward man:

column.name: text
column.value: But I see another law in my members, warring against the law of my mind, and bringing me into captivity to the law of sin which is in my members.

column.name: text
column.value: O wretched man that I am! who shall deliver me from the body of this death?

column.name: text
column.value: I thank God through Jesus Christ our Lord. So then with the mind I myself serve the law of God; but with the flesh the law of sin.

column.name: text
column.value: Brethren, my heart's desire and prayer to God for Israel is, that they may be saved.

column.name: text
column.value: For I bear them witness that they have a zeal of God, but not according to knowledge.

column.name: text
column.value: For they being ignorant of God's righteousness, and seeking to establish their own righteousness, have not submitted themselves to the righteousness of God.

column.name: text
column.value: For Christ {is} the end of the law for righteousness to every one that believeth.

column.name: text
column.value: For Moses describeth the righteousness which is by the law, That the man who doeth those things shall live by them.

column.name: text
column.value: But the righteousness which is by faith speaketh on this wise, Say not in thy heart, Who shall ascend into heaven? (that is, to bring Christ down:)

column.name: text
column.value: Or, Who shall descend into the deep? (that is, to bring Christ again from the dead.)

column.name: text
column.value: But what saith it? The word is near thee, {even} in thy mouth, and in thy heart: that is, the word of faith, which we preach;

column.name: text
column.value: That if thou shalt confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and shalt believe in thy heart that God hath raised him from the dead, thou shalt be saved.

column.name: text
column.value: For with the heart man believeth to righteousness; and with the mouth confession is made to salvation.

column.name: text
column.value: For the scripture saith, Whoever believeth on him shall not be ashamed.

column.name: text
column.value: For there is no difference between the Jew and the Greek: for the same Lord over all is rich to all that call upon him.

column.name: text
column.value: For whoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved.

column.name: text
column.value: How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? and how shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard? and how shall they hear without a preacher?

column.name: text
column.value: And how shall they preach, except they be sent? as it is written, How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace, and bring glad tidings of good things!

column.name: text
column.value: But they have not all obeyed the gospel. For Isaiah saith, Lord, who hath believed our report?

column.name: text
column.value: So then faith {cometh} by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.

column.name: text
column.value: But I say, Have they not heard? Yes verily, their sound went into all the earth, and their words to the ends of the world.

column.name: text
column.value: But I say, Did not Israel know? First Moses saith, I will provoke you to jealousy by {them that are} no people, {and} by a foolish nation I will anger you.

column.name: text
column.value: But Isaiah is very bold, and saith, I was found by them that sought me not; I was made manifest to them that asked not for me.

column.name: text
column.value: But to Israel he saith, All day long I have stretched forth my hands to a disobedient and contrary people.

column.name: text
column.value: {There is} therefore now no condemnation to them who are in Christ Jesus, who walk not according to the flesh, but according to the Spirit.

column.name: text
column.value: For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus hath made me free from the law of sin and death.

column.name: text
column.value: For what the law could not do, in that it was weak through the flesh, God sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh, and for sin, condemned sin in the flesh:

column.name: text
column.value: That the righteousness of the law may be fulfilled in us, who walk not according to the flesh, but according to the Spirit.

column.name: text
column.value: For they that are according to the flesh do mind the things of the flesh; but they that are according to the Spirit the things of the Spirit.

column.name: text
column.value: For to be carnally minded {is} death; but to be spiritually minded {is} life and peace.

column.name: text
column.value: Because the carnal mind {is} enmity against God: for it is not subject to the law of God, neither indeed can be.

column.name: text
column.value: So then they that are in the flesh cannot please God.

column.name: text
column.value: But ye are not in the flesh, but in the Spirit, if the Spirit of God dwelleth in you. Now if any man hath not the Spirit of Christ, he is not his.

column.name: text
column.value: And if Christ {is} in you, the body {is} dead because of sin; but the Spirit {is} life because of righteousness.

column.name: text
column.value: But if the Spirit of him that raised Jesus from the dead dwelleth in you, he that raised Christ from the dead shall also give life to your mortal bodies by his Spirit that dwelleth in you.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore, brethren, we are debtors, not to the flesh, to live according to the flesh.

column.name: text
column.value: For if ye live according to the flesh, ye shall die: but if ye through the Spirit mortify the deeds of the body, ye shall live.

column.name: text
column.value: For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God.

column.name: text
column.value: For ye have not received the spirit of bondage again to fear; but ye have received the Spirit of adoption, by which we cry, Abba, Father.

column.name: text
column.value: The Spirit himself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God:

column.name: text
column.value: And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with {him}, that we may be glorified together.

column.name: text
column.value: For I reckon that the sufferings of this present time {are} not worthy {to be compared} with the glory which shall be revealed in us.

column.name: text
column.value: For the earnest expectation of the creation waiteth for the revealing of the sons of God.

column.name: text
column.value: For the creation was made subject to vanity, not willingly, but by reason of him who hath subjected {the same} in hope,

column.name: text
column.value: Because the creation itself also shall be delivered from the bondage of corruption into the glorious liberty of the children of God.

column.name: text
column.value: For we know that the whole creation groaneth and travaileth in pain together until now.

column.name: text
column.value: And not only {they}, but ourselves also, who have the firstfruits of the Spirit, even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for the adoption, {that is}, the redemption of our body.

column.name: text
column.value: For we are saved by hope: but hope that is seen is not hope: for what a man seeth, why doth he yet hope for?

column.name: text
column.value: But if we hope for what we see not, {then} with patience we wait for {it}.

column.name: text
column.value: Likewise the Spirit also helpeth our infirmity: for we know not what we should pray for as we ought: but the Spirit himself maketh intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered.

column.name: text
column.value: And he that searcheth the hearts knoweth what {is} the mind of the Spirit, because he maketh intercession for the saints according to {the will of} God.

column.name: text
column.value: And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to {his} purpose.

column.name: text
column.value: For whom he did foreknow, he also did predestinate {to be} conformed to the image of his Son, that he might be the firstborn among many brethren.

column.name: text
column.value: Moreover whom he did predestinate, them he also called: and whom he called, them he also justified: and whom he justified, them he also glorified.

column.name: text
column.value: What shall we then say to these things? If God {is} for us, who {can be} against us?

column.name: text
column.value: He that spared not his own Son, but delivered him up for us all, how shall he not with him also freely give us all things?

column.name: text
column.value: Who shall lay any thing to the charge of God's elect? {It is} God that justifieth.

column.name: text
column.value: Who {is} he that condemneth? {It is} Christ that died, or rather, that is risen again, who is even at the right hand of God, who also maketh intercession for us.

column.name: text
column.value: What shall separate us from the love of Christ? {shall} tribulation, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or peril, or sword?

column.name: text
column.value: As it is written, For thy sake we are killed all the day long; we are accounted as sheep for the slaughter.

column.name: text
column.value: But, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him that loved us.

column.name: text
column.value: For I am persuaded, that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come,

column.name: text
column.value: Nor height, nor depth, nor any other created thing, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.

column.name: text
column.value: I say the truth in Christ, I lie not, my conscience also bearing me witness in the Holy Spirit,

column.name: text
column.value: That I have great heaviness and continual sorrow in my heart.

column.name: text
column.value: For I could wish that myself were accursed from Christ for my brethren, my kinsmen according to the flesh:

column.name: text
column.value: Who are Israelites; to whom {pertain} the adoption, and the glory, and the covenants, and the giving of the law, and the service {of God}, and the promises;

column.name: text
column.value: Whose {are} the fathers, and from whom according to the flesh Christ {came}, who is over all, God blessed for ever. Amen.

column.name: text
column.value: Not as though the word of God hath taken no effect. For they {are} not all Israel, who are descended from Israel:

column.name: text
column.value: Neither, because they are the seed of Abraham, {are they} all children: but, In Isaac shall thy seed be called.

column.name: text
column.value: That is, They who are the children of the flesh, these {are} not the children of God: but the children of the promise are counted for the seed.

column.name: text
column.value: For this {is} the word of promise, At this time will I come, and Sarah shall have a son.

column.name: text
column.value: And not only {this}; but when Rebecca also had conceived by one, {even} by our father Isaac;

column.name: text
column.value: (For {the children} being not yet born, neither having done any good or evil, that the purpose of God according to election might stand, not of works, but of him that calleth;)

column.name: text
column.value: It was said to her, The elder shall serve the younger.

column.name: text
column.value: As it is written, Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated.

column.name: text
column.value: What shall we say then? {Is there} unrighteousness with God? By no means.

column.name: text
column.value: For he saith to Moses, I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I will have compassion.

column.name: text
column.value: So then {it is} not of him that willeth, nor of him that runneth, but of God that showeth mercy.

column.name: text
column.value: For the scripture saith to Pharaoh, Even for this same purpose have I raised thee up, that I might show my power in thee, and that my name might be declared throughout all the earth.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore he hath mercy on whom he will {have mercy}, and whom he will he hardeneth.

column.name: text
column.value: Thou wilt say then to me, Why doth he yet find fault? For who hath resisted his will?

column.name: text
column.value: Nay but, O man, who art thou that repliest against God? Shall the thing formed say to him that formed {it}, Why hast thou made me thus?

column.name: text
column.value: Hath not the potter power over the clay, of the same lump to make one vessel to honour, and another to dishonour?

column.name: text
column.value: {What} if God, willing to show {his} wrath, and to make his power known, endured with much longsuffering the vessels of wrath fitted to destruction:

column.name: text
column.value: And that he might make known the riches of his glory on the vessels of mercy, which he had before prepared for glory,

column.name: text
column.value: Even us, whom he hath called, not of the Jews only, but also of the Gentiles?

column.name: text
column.value: As he saith also in Hosea, I will call them my people, who were not my people; and her beloved, who was not beloved.

column.name: text
